questions.question_text: A person falls on the lateral side of the arm and subsequently cannot extend the wrist, cannot make a strong hand grip, and has loss of sensation on the dorsum of the hand and fingers. Which structure is involved?
questions.explanation: The source identifies radial nerve injury. It describes wrist drop due to paralysis of wrist extensors, reduced grip strength due to loss of synergy between wrist extensors and finger flexors, and sensory deficit over the posterior lateral arm and dorsum of the hand.

questions.question_text: The epiglottis develops from which of the following structures?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the fourth pharyngeal arch as the origin of the epiglottis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following muscles is NOT involved in damage to the cranial part of the accessory nerve?
questions.explanation: The source identifies stylopharyngeus as the answer.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Hypothalamus is part of the brainstem
Occipital lobe is part of the cerebral cortex
Medulla is part of the limbic system

questions.explanation: The source identifies the occipital lobe as part of the cerebral cortex.

questions.question_text: A cervical vertebra is differentiated from a thoracic vertebra by the presence of:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the foramen transversarium as the distinguishing feature.

questions.question_text: Which nerve nucleus underlies the facial colliculus?
questions.explanation: The source states that the facial colliculus is situated in the pons and overlies the abducent nucleus. The facial nerve fibers loop around the abducent nucleus.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about cavernous sinus thrombosis except:

options.text: It most commonly spreads through the ethmoid sinus
Loss of sensation around the orbit
Infection can spread to the cavernous sinus from the danger area of the face via the inferior ophthalmic vein

questions.explanation: The source identifies loss of jaw jerk as the exception. It describes spread of infection from the face and paranasal sinuses through venous connections, including the ophthalmic veins, and lists involvement of cranial nerves III, IV, V and VI, proptosis, chemosis and reduced sensation in the ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve.

questions.question_text: Membrana tectoria is a continuation of which structure?
questions.explanation: The source describes the membrana tectoria as a prolongation upward of the posterior longitudinal ligament. It covers the dens and its ligaments and lies posterior to the transverse ligament.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about the sphincter urethrae except:
questions.explanation: The source identifies location at the bladder neck as the exception. It describes the external urethral sphincter as voluntary, striated muscle, supplied by the perineal branch of the pudendal nerve (S2–S4), and arising from the ischiopubic rami. The internal urethral sphincter is located at the bladder neck.

questions.question_text: When pronation of the foot occurs, the axes of which joints move in a parallel direction?
questions.explanation: The source states that as the subtalar joint pronates, the longitudinal axis of the talonavicular joint and the oblique axis of the calcaneocuboid joint become parallel.

questions.question_text: The term 'Turkish saddle' refers to:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the pituitary gland. The sella turcica is a depression at the base of the skull in which the pituitary gland is situated.

questions.question_text: All of the following are made of dense collagen except:
questions.explanation: The source identifies periosteum as the exception and states that tendons, ligaments and aponeuroses are formed by dense regular connective tissue.

questions.question_text: All of the following sensations are carried by the dorsal column except:
questions.explanation: The source identifies pain as the exception. The dorsal columns carry proprioceptive, touch, pressure and vibratory sensations.

questions.question_text: All of the following are derived from ectoderm except:
questions.explanation: The source identifies arrector pili as the exception. It describes arrector pili as a smooth muscle in the dermis derived from mesoderm.
references: Human Embryology and Developmental Biology, Carlson, 5th edition, Chapter 9

questions.question_text: Which of the following muscles is NOT a derivative of mesoderm?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the dilator muscles of the pupil as the answer. It states that the sphincter and dilator pupillae muscles of the iris are ectodermal in origin.

questions.question_text: Venous drainage of the esophagus is into the:

options.text: Azygos, inferior thyroid and left gastric veins
Azygos, inferior thyroid and right gastric veins
Superior thyroid, inferior thyroid, azygos and hemiazygos veins

questions.explanation: The source identifies the azygos, inferior thyroid and left gastric veins. It describes drainage from the cervical esophagus into the inferior thyroid vein, thoracic esophagus into the azygos system, and abdominal esophagus into the left gastric vein.

questions.question_text: The most common variant in the blood supply of the colon is:
questions.explanation: The source identifies an absent right colic artery as the most common variant. It notes that the right colic artery is highly variable and may arise from a common trunk with the middle colic artery, separately from the superior mesenteric artery, from the ileocolic artery, or may be absent.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT true about the blood-testis barrier?

options.text: It is formed by Sertoli cells
It is formed before primary spermatogenesis
Rupture of the barrier can cause an immune response to germ cells
Germ cells are not necessary for formation of the barrier

questions.explanation: The source identifies the statement that the barrier is formed before primary spermatogenesis as NOT true. It states that the barrier is formed by Sertoli cells, germ cells are not necessary for its formation, and rupture can cause an immune response to germ cells.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT true about the dura mater?

options.text: It is the outermost layer of the cranial meninges
It has periosteal and meningeal layers
Dural venous sinuses lie below the meningeal layer
It is supplied by a branch of the fifth cranial nerve

questions.explanation: The source identifies option C as the incorrect statement. It explains that dural venous sinuses lie between the outer endosteal (periosteal) and inner meningeal layers of the dura mater.

questions.question_text: Which of the following structures is seen in the cavernous sinus?

options.text: Maxillary division of the trigeminal nerve
Mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve

questions.explanation: The source identifies the internal carotid artery as the answer. It lists the internal carotid artery and abducent nerve within the sinus, with the oculomotor, trochlear and ophthalmic nerves in its lateral wall.

questions.question_text: The medulla receives its blood supply from all of the following arteries except:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the superior cerebellar artery as the exception. It lists the anterior spinal artery, branches of the vertebral artery and posterior inferior cerebellar artery as supplying the medulla.

questions.question_text: Which of the following muscles is supplied by the contralateral nerve nucleus?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the superior rectus. It states that the superior rectus and superior oblique muscles are supplied by the opposite-side nuclei of the third and fourth cranial nerves, respectively.

questions.question_text: The trigeminal nerve supplies all of the following muscles except:
questions.explanation: The source identifies stylohyoid as the exception. It explains that the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve supplies muscles derived from the first pharyngeal arch, including the medial and lateral pterygoids and tensor veli palatini.

questions.question_text: The facial nerve gives secretomotor fibres to all of the following except:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the parotid gland as the exception. It states that the parotid gland receives parasympathetic secretomotor innervation from preganglionic fibres arising in the inferior salivatory nucleus.

questions.question_text: Pronator teres syndrome is related to which nerve?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the median nerve.

questions.question_text: Purkinje cells of the cerebellum are connected to:
questions.explanation: The source identifies all of the above. Its accompanying explanation describes climbing fibres and mossy fibres as the two main inputs to the cerebellar cortex, and notes that climbing fibres project directly to the primary dendrites of Purkinje cells.

questions.question_text: The right superior intercostal vein drains into:
questions.explanation: The source states that the right superior intercostal vein drains into the azygos vein. It also notes that the left superior intercostal vein drains into the left brachiocephalic vein or azygos vein.

questions.question_text: The vaginal wall is derived from which of the following?
questions.explanation: The source identifies endoderm of the urogenital sinus. Its explanation states that the upper two-thirds of the vagina develops from the uterovaginal canal, while the lower one-third develops from the sinovaginal bulb derived from the urogenital sinus.

questions.question_text: Which of the following structures pass through the superior orbital fissure?
questions.explanation: The source identifies all of the above. It lists the oculomotor nerve among the structures passing through the middle part, and the trochlear nerve and superior ophthalmic vein among those passing through the lateral part of the superior orbital fissure.

questions.question_text: Which nerve is transmitted through Dorello's canal at the tip of the temporal bone?

options.text: Superior alveolar branch of maxillary nerve

questions.explanation: The source identifies the abducent nerve (sixth cranial nerve) as the structure transmitted through Dorello's canal.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a holocrine gland?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the sebaceous gland as holocrine because its secretion contains the entire secreting cells. It describes sweat glands as merocrine or apocrine and the breast as a modified sweat gland of apocrine type.

questions.question_text: Which muscle is described as the 'forgotten rotator cuff muscle'?
questions.explanation: The source identifies subscapularis as the forgotten rotator cuff muscle and describes its importance in glenohumeral stability.

questions.question_text: Which of the following structures is NOT present on the floor of the third ventricle?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the third nerve (oculomotor nerve) as not forming the floor of the third ventricle. It lists the optic chiasma, tuber cinereum, infundibulum and mammillary bodies among the structures forming the floor.

questions.question_text: Which of the following does NOT contribute to the boundaries of the facial recess?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the stapedius tendon as the answer. It describes the facial recess as bounded medially by the vertical part of the facial nerve, laterally by the chorda tympani and above by the fossa incudis.

questions.question_text: The urethral crest is an elevation seen in the urethra due to:
questions.explanation: The source identifies prostatic glands. It describes the urethral crest as a longitudinal ridge on the posterior wall of the prostatic urethra, with prostatic ducts opening into the adjacent prostatic sinuses.

questions.question_text: Which of the following does NOT contribute to the formation of the anorectal ring in human beings?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the anococcygeal raphe as the answer. It states that the anorectal ring is formed by the puborectalis, uppermost fibres of the external anal sphincter and internal anal sphincter.

questions.question_text: All of the following bones form parts of the inferior wall of the orbit except:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the ethmoid bone as the exception. It states that the inferior wall of the orbit consists of the zygomatic, maxillary and palatine bones.

questions.question_text: Lacrimation is affected due to damage to which of the following nerves?
questions.explanation: The greater petrosal nerve is a branch of the facial nerve. It carries secretomotor fibres to the pterygopalatine ganglion. Postganglionic fibres innervate the lacrimal gland and are responsible for tear formation. Damage can lead to absence of tears.

questions.question_text: While performing drainage of fluid from the pleural cavity, the needle is introduced through all of the following structures except:
questions.explanation: The pleural space lies between the parietal pleura and visceral (pulmonary) pleura. The parietal pleura is pierced to reach the pleural space for fluid drainage; the visceral pleura is not pierced.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the only complete cartilage ring in the respiratory tree?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the cricoid cartilage as the only complete cartilage ring. It encircles the larynx below the thyroid cartilage.

questions.question_text: The lower two parts of the sternal body are fused by:
questions.explanation: The source states that the lower two parts of the sternal body are fused by 14 years.

questions.question_text: Oogonia at the time of birth are present in which of the following stages of meiosis?
questions.explanation: The source states that meiosis I begins during embryonic development and is halted in the diplotene stage of prophase I until puberty.

questions.question_text: All of the following are branches of the external carotid artery except:
questions.explanation: The transverse cervical artery is a branch of the thyrocervical trunk, not the external carotid artery.

questions.question_text: Which of the following muscles is NOT inserted into the greater tubercle of the humerus?
questions.explanation: The subscapularis muscle is inserted into the lesser tubercle of the humerus. The supraspinatus, infraspinatus and teres minor are inserted into the greater tubercle.

questions.question_text: The card test is done for which of the following muscles?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the palmar interossei as the muscle group assessed by the card test.

questions.question_text: In which of the following are microvilli NOT present?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the collecting duct. It states that microvilli form a striated border in absorptive surfaces of small intestinal epithelial cells and a less regular brush border in gallbladder epithelium and proximal kidney tubules.

questions.question_text: Independent assortment of maternal and paternal chromosomes occurs at which stage of spermatocyte maturation?
questions.explanation: The source states that independent assortment of paternal and maternal chromosomes occurs during meiosis I, when a primary spermatocyte is converted into two secondary spermatocytes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a support of the uterus?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the rectovaginal septum as not being a support of the uterus. It lists the pelvic diaphragm and perineal body among the muscular or active supports, along with ligamentous supports.

questions.question_text: All of the following are derived from the mesonephros except:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the glomerulus as the exception. It lists the vas deferens and epididymis among structures derived from the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct.

questions.question_text: In gene studies, the specific site to which the enzyme CRE recombinase binds is:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the LoxP site. Cre-Lox recombination is a site-specific recombinase technology in which Cre recombinase acts on paired Lox target sequences.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a content of the mesorectal fascia?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the inferior rectal vein as the exception. It lists the superior rectal artery and vein, lymphatic vessels and nodes, branches from the inferior mesenteric plexus, and loose adipose connective tissue among the contents.

questions.question_text: Reticular fibres of collagen tissues are present in all of the following except:
questions.explanation: The source states that reticular fibres are present in the spleen, bone marrow and lymph node, but not in the thymus. It describes reticulin as type III collagen secreted by reticular cells.

questions.question_text: Sensory supply of the cornea is by which of the following?

options.text: Nasolacrimal nerve (probably printing mistake - probably Nasociliary nerve)

questions.explanation: The source marks option D but explicitly notes a probable printing mistake, suggesting Nasociliary nerve instead of Nasolacrimal nerve. It explains that the cornea receives sensory supply mainly through long ciliary nerves, which are branches of the nasociliary nerve.

questions.question_text: All of the following have general visceral efferent fibres except:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the olfactory nerve as not having general visceral efferent fibres.

questions.question_text: In a study to detect extracellular fluid volume, 10 gm mannitol was injected by intravenous route and after waiting for adequate time for equilibration of levels, concentration was measured as 50 mg/100 ml. In this time, 10% mannitol was excreted. What is the calculated volume of ECF?
questions.explanation: The source calculates that 10% of the injected 10 g mannitol was excreted, leaving 9 g distributed in the ECF. Given a concentration of 50 mg/100 ml, ECF volume = amount/concentration = 9 g ÷ 50 mg × 100 ml = 18 L.

questions.question_text: A 37-year-old patient presented with hyperextension of the 4th and 5th metacarpophalangeal joints with flexion at the proximal interphalangeal joints. This deformity is due to injury to:
questions.explanation: The source identifies injury to the deep branch of the ulnar nerve. It describes the deformity as claw hand.
references: Gray's Anatomy, 41st edition, pages 784 and 866; 40th edition, page 888

questions.question_text: Which of the following nerves supplies the ear lobule?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the greater auricular nerve as supplying the ear lobule. It also describes its supply to most of the cranial surface and posterior part of the lateral surface of the auricle.
references: Gray's Anatomy, 41st edition, page 627; 40th edition, page 620

questions.question_text: Which of the following structures is NOT involved in the development of the diaphragm?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the pleuropericardial membrane as not being involved in diaphragm formation. It lists the septum transversum, pleuroperitoneal membranes, mesentery of the oesophagus and body wall as contributors.

questions.question_text: Which of these is an immune-privileged site?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the seminiferous tubules of the testis as an immune-privileged site. It also lists the placenta and fetus, brain and anterior chamber of the eye as immune-privileged sites.

questions.question_text: The craniovertebral joint does NOT include:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the wings of the sphenoid as the exception. It describes the craniovertebral joint as involving the occipital condyles, atlas and axis.

questions.question_text: The maxillary bone does NOT articulate with:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the sphenoid as the answer. It states that the maxilla articulates with the frontal, ethmoid, nasal, zygomatic, lacrimal, inferior nasal concha, palatine, vomer and adjacent fused maxilla.
references: Gray's Anatomy, 41st edition, page 484; 40th edition, pages 473–476

questions.question_text: True statements about osteoblasts are all except:

options.text: Have a plasma membrane showing multiple folds

questions.explanation: The source identifies a plasma membrane showing multiple folds as the exception. It explains that the ruffled border is a characteristic of active osteoclasts involved in bone resorption, whereas osteoblasts are derived from osteoprogenitor cells and are stimulated by bone morphogenetic proteins.

questions.question_text: Which of the following vessels supply the anal canal?
questions.explanation: The source identifies all of the listed arteries. It states that the anal canal receives supply from the superior rectal, middle rectal and inferior rectal arteries, and occasionally from the median sacral artery.
references: Gray's Anatomy, 41st edition, page 1058; 40th edition, pages 1155–1159
Manual of Total Mesorectal Excision, Moran, Richard John Heald (2013), page 40

questions.question_text: Buccinator is pierced by all of the following except:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the buccal branch of the mandibular nerve as the answer. Its explanation also states that the buccal branch of the facial nerve crosses the buccinator and innervates it without piercing it.
references: Gray's Anatomy, 41st edition, page 487; 40th edition, page 487

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about the location of the otic ganglion except:
questions.explanation: The source identifies 'lateral to mandibular nerve' as the incorrect statement. It explains that the mandibular nerve lies lateral to the otic ganglion, meaning the ganglion lies medial to the mandibular nerve.
references: Gray's Anatomy, 41st edition, page 552; 40th edition, page 543

questions.question_text: What is the most important blood supply to the stomach?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the left gastric artery as the largest artery supplying the stomach. It is a branch of the coeliac trunk. Other listed gastric blood supplies arise from the splenic, hepatic and gastroduodenal arteries.

questions.question_text: In spermatogenesis, independent assortment of paternal and maternal chromosomes occurs during:
questions.explanation: The source states that independent assortment of paternal and maternal chromosomes occurs during meiosis I, when a primary spermatocyte is converted into two secondary spermatocytes.

questions.question_text: Buccopharyngeal membrane develops from:
questions.explanation: The buccopharyngeal and cloacal membranes are regions where ectoderm and underlying endoderm are opposed without intervening mesoblast. The two layers come into direct contact to form the thin buccopharyngeal membrane.

questions.question_text: Epithelioid cells include which of the following:
questions.explanation: The source identifies both islet cells of the pancreas and interstitial cells of Leydig as epithelioid cells. Epithelioid tissues resemble epithelia but lack a characteristic free surface; their cells are closely associated, like cells of a true epithelium.

questions.question_text: All of the following bones are involved in wrist joint formation, except:
questions.explanation: The radiocarpal joint is formed by the distal end of the radius and the articular disc above, and the scaphoid, lunate and triquetral bones below. The ulna is excluded from the wrist joint by the articular disc.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cranial nerves is NOT associated with olfaction?
questions.explanation: The source identifies cranial nerve XII (hypoglossal nerve) as the answer. It states that the hypoglossal nerve is a motor nerve and does not play a role in olfaction or gustation.

questions.question_text: Ligamentum flavum consists of:
questions.explanation: Ligamentum flavum connects the laminae of adjacent vertebrae and has a high content of elastin. The source states that it can be stretched by 80% under tension without damage and helps maintain a smooth lining to the vertebral canal.

questions.question_text: Golgi apparatus in serous acinar cells is at:
questions.explanation: The source states that serous cells have a pyramidal shape, abundant rough endoplasmic reticulum, a supranuclear Golgi complex and numerous spherical secretory granules.

questions.question_text: What is the location of Meissner's corpuscles?
questions.explanation: Meissner corpuscles are encapsulated nerve endings present in the dermal papillae. The source also notes that Merkel cells are located in the stratum basale and Pacinian corpuscles in the reticular layer of the dermis.

questions.question_text: Which curvature is normally seen in the lumbar spine?
questions.explanation: The source identifies lordosis as the normal lumbar curvature. Its explanation describes increased lumbar curvature as lordosis, lateral deviation as scoliosis and increased thoracic curvature as kyphosis.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about the grey ramus communicans except:

options.text: Present medial to the white ramus communicans

questions.explanation: The source identifies 'preganglionic' as the exception. Grey rami communicantes contain postganglionic sympathetic fibres, which are largely unmyelinated. They connect the sympathetic trunk or ganglion to the anterior ramus of a spinal nerve.

questions.question_text: Parasympathetic nervous system comprises of:

options.text: Cranial nerves III, V, VII, X and sacral nerves S1, S2, S3, S4, S5
Cranial nerves III, VII, IX, X and sacral nerves S2, S3, S4
Cranial nerves V, VII, IX, X and sacral nerves S2, S3, S4
Cranial nerves III, V, VII, X and sacral nerves S2, S3, S4

questions.explanation: The source describes parasympathetic outflow as craniosacral, carried by cranial nerves III, VII, IX and X, and sacral nerves S2, S3 and S4.

questions.question_text: Extra-embryonic mesoderm is derived from:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the primary yolk sac as the origin of extra-embryonic mesoderm. It states that it is formed by delamination of yolk sac cells and later by migration of cells through the primitive streak during gastrulation.
references: Gray's Anatomy, 41st edition, page 169; 40th edition, pages 167, 173 and 186–189
Langman's Medical Embryology, 13th edition, page 45; 12th edition, pages 54–55

questions.question_text: The anterior two-thirds of the tongue is demarcated from the posterior one-third by:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the sulcus terminalis as the boundary. It describes this as a V-shaped sulcus dividing the tongue into an anterior oral (presulcal) part and a posterior pharyngeal (postsulcal) part.
references: Gray's Anatomy, 41st edition, page 511; 40th edition, page 503

questions.question_text: All of the following structures lie in relation to the left ureter except:
questions.explanation: The source identifies quadratus lumborum as the exception. It states that the left ureter is related posteriorly to the psoas major muscle, not quadratus lumborum. Its anterior relations include the sigmoid colon, sigmoid mesocolon, left colic vessels and left gonadal vessels.
references: Gray's Anatomy, 41st edition, page 1251; 40th edition, page 1239

questions.question_text: All of the following muscles have parallel-oriented fibers except:
questions.explanation: The source identifies tibialis anterior as the exception. Sartorius, rectus abdominis and sternohyoid have parallel-oriented fibers, whereas tibialis anterior is described as a multipennate muscle with oblique fibers.
references: Gray's Anatomy, 41st edition, page 112; 40th edition, pages 104–105

questions.question_text: What is the nerve supply of the angle of the jaw?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the greater auricular nerve. It states that the skin over the angle of the mandible is supplied by this nerve, which carries branches from the anterior rami of C2 and C3.
references: Gray's Anatomy, 41st edition, pages 407 and 413; 40th edition, page 435

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about venous drainage of the esophagus except:

options.text: Thoracic esophagus drains into the azygos vein
Esophageal veins drain into a submucosal plexus
The cervical esophagus drains directly into the right brachiocephalic vein
Lower esophageal veins anastomose with the left gastric vein

questions.explanation: The source identifies the statement about direct drainage into the right brachiocephalic vein as incorrect. It states that the cervical esophagus drains into the inferior thyroid vein, the thoracic part into the azygos and hemiazygos veins, and the abdominal part through venous channels including the left gastric vein.
references: Gray's Anatomy, 41st edition, page 1111; 40th edition, page 950

questions.question_text: Type I collagen is present in all except:
questions.explanation: The source identifies cartilage as the exception and states that cartilage contains type II collagen. It lists type I collagen in bone, skin, dentin, cornea, tendons and ligaments.
references: Ross and Pawlina, Histology: A Text and Atlas, 7th edition, pages 160–167

questions.question_text: Which compartment of the leg does NOT have a neurovascular bundle?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the superficial posterior compartment as the answer. It lists gastrocnemius, plantaris and soleus in the superficial part of the posterior compartment, while the deep part contains muscles along with the posterior tibial and peroneal vessels and tibial nerve.

questions.question_text: At what level does the spinal cord end in adults?
questions.explanation: The source states that the adult spinal cord terminates on average at the middle third of the body of the first lumbar vertebra, approximately corresponding to the transpyloric plane.

questions.question_text: The inferior thyroid artery is a branch of:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the thyrocervical trunk as the origin of the inferior thyroid artery. The thyrocervical trunk arises from the first part of the subclavian artery and divides into the inferior thyroid, suprascapular and superficial cervical arteries.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sensations is NOT perceived by the spinal nucleus of the trigeminal nerve?
questions.explanation: The source identifies proprioception as the answer. It explains that proprioceptive impulses from the muscles of mastication and facial and extraocular muscles are carried by fibres whose cell bodies are in the mesencephalic nucleus of the trigeminal nerve.
references: Barr's The Human Nervous System, 10th edition, page 127

questions.question_text: Purkinje fibers relay to which of the following?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the dentate nucleus. It explains that the axons of cerebellar Purkinje cells pass to and synapse with neurons of the cerebellar nuclei, including the fastigial, globose, emboliform and dentate nuclei.
references: Barr's The Human Nervous System, 10th edition, page 164

questions.question_text: Which of the following is false regarding the blood supply of the dura mater?

options.text: Meningeal branch of ICA in posterior cranial fossa
Meningeal branch of anterior and posterior ethmoidal artery

questions.explanation: The source identifies option C as false. However, its explanation subsequently lists anterior meningeal branches of the anterior and posterior ethmoidal arteries as supplying the anterior cranial fossa. The source therefore contains a contradiction between the keyed answer and its explanation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about the nerve supply of the adrenal gland?

options.text: Release of catecholamines is not affected by nerve supply to adrenals
Preganglionic fibres from lower thoracic and lumbar vertebra come via sympathetic chain to supply adrenals
Adrenal cortex doesn't have nerve supply as it has endocrine functions
Adrenal medulla doesn't have nerve supply

questions.explanation: The source identifies option B. It describes the suprarenal gland as having substantial autonomic supply, including predominantly preganglionic sympathetic fibres originating in lower thoracic spinal segments and reaching the suprarenal plexus via branches of the greater splanchnic nerves.

questions.question_text: Which finger has two dorsal interossei attached?
questions.explanation: The source states that the second and third dorsal interossei attach to either side of the third (middle) finger. The first attaches to the lateral side of the index finger, and the fourth to the medial side of the ring finger.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following structures in sequence from lateral to medial.
questions.explanation: The source gives the sequence as cochlear nucleus → lateral lemniscus → inferior colliculus → medial geniculate body. It presents this as part of the auditory pathway.

questions.question_text: Which is NOT a branch of the external carotid artery supplying the nasal septum?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the anterior ethmoidal artery as the answer. It explains that the sphenopalatine, greater palatine, superior labial and angular arteries arise from the external carotid system, while the anterior and posterior ethmoidal arteries arise from the ophthalmic artery, which is a branch of the internal carotid artery.

questions.question_text:
Mark true or false among the following statements about the contents of the carotid sheath:
A. Internal jugular vein
B. Cervical sympathetic trunk
C. Vagus nerve
D. Internal carotid artery
E. Deep cervical lymph nodes

options.text: A. False; B. False; C. True; D. True; E. True
A. True; B. False; C. False; D. True; E. True
A. True; B. False; C. True; D. True; E. False
A. True; B. False; C. True; D. True; E. True

questions.explanation: The source identifies option D. The carotid sheath contains the internal jugular vein, common and internal carotid arteries, vagus nerve and deep cervical lymph nodes. The cervical sympathetic trunk lies behind the sheath and is not included within it.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about levator ani except:

options.text: Made up of iliococcygeus and pubococcygeus

questions.explanation: The source identifies attachment to the pelvic brim as the exception. It describes levator ani as comprising iliococcygeus, pubococcygeus and puborectalis, with fibres passing downward and backward towards the pelvic floor. Its action includes supporting the pelvic viscera.

questions.question_text: Couinaud classified the liver into 8 segments. Which structure differentiates the segments anatomically?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the hepatic veins. It states that hepatic veins lie at the periphery of each segment, while branches of the portal veins, hepatic arteries and bile ducts are centrally located. The middle hepatic vein divides the liver into right and left lobes.

questions.question_text:
Assertion: The distal pole of the scaphoid undergoes avascular necrosis after a scaphoid fracture.
Reason: The blood supply of the scaphoid is from distal to proximal.

options.text: Assertion is true but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion
Both assertion and reason are false
Reason is true but assertion is false

questions.explanation: The source states that the reason is true but the assertion is false. The scaphoid has a retrograde blood supply: the proximal pole relies on intramedullary blood flow and is especially prone to non-union and avascular necrosis after fracture.

questions.question_text: Golgi tendon organs are used to detect:
questions.explanation: The source describes the Golgi tendon organ as a proprioceptive sensory receptor that detects changes in muscle tension. It lies at the origins and insertions of skeletal muscle fibres into their tendons.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is false about the innervation of the parotid gland?

options.text: Preganglionic parasympathetic fibre relays in the otic ganglion
Preganglionic parasympathetic nerve begins in the inferior petrosal nucleus

questions.explanation: The source identifies option C as false. It lists the auriculotemporal nerve in the parasympathetic supply and a plexus around the external carotid artery in the sympathetic supply. The source does not provide further detail about the origin of the preganglionic parasympathetic fibres.

questions.question_text:
Arrange the following layers of the epidermis from surface to deep layer:
Corneocytes
Merkel cells
Melanocytes
Langerhans cells

options.text: Corneocytes > Merkel cells > Melanocytes > Langerhans cells
Merkel cells > Corneocytes > Melanocytes > Langerhans cells
Melanocytes > Merkel cells > Corneocytes > Langerhans cells
Corneocytes > Langerhans cells > Melanocytes > Merkel cells

questions.explanation: The source gives option D. Its explanation places corneocytes in the superficial cornified layer, Langerhans cells in the middle of the spinous layer, and melanocytes and Merkel cells in the basal layer.

questions.question_text: Which part of the brachial plexus does NOT give branches?
questions.explanation: The source states that divisions of the brachial plexus do not give branches.

questions.question_text: Maximum contribution to the floor of orbit is by:
questions.explanation: The maxillae jointly form the whole of the upper jaw. Each bone forms the greater part of the floor and lateral wall of the nasal cavity and of the floor of the orbit. The orbital surface of the maxilla forms most of the floor of the orbit.

questions.question_text: Structures passing through Calot's triangle are all EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The boundaries of the hepatobiliary or Calot's triangle are the common hepatic duct medially, cystic duct inferiorly, and inferior surface of the liver superiorly. Its contents include the cystic artery, right hepatic artery, and lymph node of Lund.

questions.question_text: Which is a typical intercostal nerve?
questions.explanation: Typical intercostal nerves are confined to their own intercostal spaces in the thoracic wall. The third, fourth, fifth, and sixth intercostal nerves are typical nerves.

questions.question_text: Trendelenburg test is positive due to injury to which of the following nerves?
questions.explanation: Gluteus medius and gluteus minimus are supplied by the superior gluteal nerve. Normally, when a person stands on one leg, the hip abductors of the ipsilateral side raise the opposite unsupported side of the pelvis. If the abductor mechanism is defective, the unsupported side of the pelvis drops, producing a positive Trendelenburg test.

questions.question_text: Lateral boundary of cubital fossa is formed by:
questions.explanation: The lateral boundary of the cubital fossa is the medial border of brachioradialis. The medial boundary is the lateral border of pronator teres. The base is an imaginary line joining the front of the two epicondyles of the humerus, and the apex is formed where brachioradialis crosses pronator teres.

questions.question_text: All of the following are structures associated with the pterygopalatine fossa, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The pterygopalatine fossa accommodates branches of the maxillary nerve (CN V2), the pterygopalatine ganglion, terminal branches of the maxillary artery, and the greater superficial petrosal nerve.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a branch of the first part of the maxillary artery?
questions.explanation: The maxillary artery has three parts. Branches of its mandibular part include the inferior alveolar, middle meningeal, deep auricular, anterior tympanic, and occasionally accessory meningeal arteries. The greater palatine artery is a branch of the pterygopalatine part.

questions.question_text: Ophthalmic artery is a branch of:
questions.explanation: The cerebral part of the internal carotid artery gives the ophthalmic artery, posterior communicating artery, anterior choroidal artery, anterior cerebral artery, and middle cerebral artery.

questions.question_text: Postganglionic fibres to the parotid gland are supplied by:
questions.explanation: Preganglionic fibres travel in the lesser petrosal branch of the glossopharyngeal nerve and synapse in the otic ganglion. Postganglionic fibres reach the parotid gland through the auriculotemporal nerve.

questions.question_text: Sensory supply to the tongue is by all, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The lingual nerve supplies general sensation to the presulcal part of the tongue and also carries taste sensation through the chorda tympani branch of the facial nerve. The glossopharyngeal nerve supplies general and taste sensation to the postsulcal part. The internal laryngeal branch of the vagus supplies an additional area near the valleculae.

questions.question_text: Cranial part of accessory nerve supplies all palatal muscles, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The cranial root of the accessory nerve innervates the pharyngeal and palatal muscles except tensor veli palatini. Tensor veli palatini is supplied by the medial pterygoid nerve, a branch of the mandibular nerve. It is the only muscle of the palate not innervated by the pharyngeal plexus.

questions.question_text: A patient is found to have a melanoma originating in the skin of the left forearm. After removal of the tumor from the forearm, all axillary lymph nodes lateral to the medial edge of the pectoralis minor muscle are removed. Which axillary nodes would not be removed?
questions.explanation: The apical axillary nodes are medial to the medial edge of pectoralis minor and therefore would not be removed. Central axillary nodes are directly under pectoralis minor. The source also describes the axillary lymph node levels in relation to the borders of pectoralis minor.

questions.question_text: A patient has a herniated intervertebral disc impinging on the right C5 nerve roots. Which of the following movements would most likely be affected?
questions.explanation: C5 helps mediate flexion, abduction, and lateral rotation of the shoulder, and flexion of the elbow. Both C5 and C6 mediate extension of the elbow. Extension of the fingers is mediated by C7 and C8; extension of the shoulder by C7 and C8; and flexion of the wrist by C6 and C7.

questions.question_text: All are true about the femoral triangle, EXCEPT:

options.text: Lateral margin is formed by sartorius
Floor is formed by adductor longus

questions.explanation: All statements are true according to the source. The femoral triangle is bounded laterally by the medial margin of sartorius, medially by the medial margin of adductor longus, and superiorly by the inguinal ligament. Its floor is formed laterally by iliacus and psoas major and medially by pectineus and adductor longus. It contains the femoral vessels.

questions.question_text: In walking, gravity tends to tilt the pelvis and trunk to the unsupported side. The major factor in preventing this unwanted movement is:
questions.explanation: Gluteus medius and gluteus minimus abduct the femur at the hip joint and hold the pelvis secure over the stance leg, preventing pelvic drop on the opposite swing side during gait.

questions.question_text: Which of the following represents the commonest variation in the arteries arising from the arch of aorta?

options.text: Left vertebral artery arising from the arch
Left common carotid artery arising from brachiocephalic trunk

questions.explanation: The source states that the most common anomaly of the aortic arch, seen in 10–20% of individuals, is characterized by the origin of the left common carotid artery from the brachiocephalic (innominate) trunk.

questions.question_text: Which among the following is NOT a branch of the arch of aorta?
questions.explanation: The three branches of the arch of aorta are the brachiocephalic artery, left common carotid artery, and left subclavian artery. The brachiocephalic artery divides into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries.

questions.question_text: The key to the root of the neck is the scalenus anterior muscle. Which among the following is TRUE about scalenus anterior?

options.text: Attached to scalene tubercle on 2nd rib
Separates subclavian artery from subclavian vein

questions.explanation: The source gives option A. The phrenic nerve passes vertically down across the obliquity of the scalenus anterior muscle, attached to it by the prevertebral fascia. Scalenus anterior attaches to the scalene tubercle and adjacent ridge on the inner border and upper surface of the first rib. The muscle separates the subclavian artery and vein.

questions.question_text: Most common diaphragmatic hernia is:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the most common diaphragmatic hernia as a posterolateral (Bochdalek) hernia. It occurs due to a defect in the posterior diaphragm in the region of the tenth or eleventh ribs.

questions.question_text: Boundary of Koch's triangle is not formed by:
questions.explanation: Koch's triangle is enclosed by the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve, the coronary sinus, and the membranous part of the interatrial septum. Its three sides are defined by the ostium of the coronary sinus, the anterior portion of the tricuspid valve annulus, and the tendon of Todaro.

questions.question_text: The esophagus is constricted at four anatomical locations. The narrowest part of the esophagus lies at which of the following constrictions?

options.text: At the level of cricopharyngeal sphincter
At the crossing of aortic arch
At the crossing of left bronchus
At the level of opening in the diaphragm

questions.explanation: The narrowest part of the esophagus is at its commencement at the cricopharyngeal sphincter, which is 15 cm from the incisor teeth. Other constrictions are at the crossing of the aortic arch (22 cm), left principal bronchus (27 cm), and opening in the diaphragm (38 cm).

questions.question_text: Sympathetic supply to the heart arises from which of the following spinal segments?
questions.explanation: Sympathetic nerve cells supplying the heart are located in the intermediolateral horn of spinal segments T1 to T5. Sympathetic supply is cardio-acceleratory and, on stimulation, increases heart rate and dilates coronary arteries.

questions.question_text: All of the following are branches of the splenic artery, except:
questions.explanation: The right gastroepiploic artery is a branch of the gastroduodenal artery. The left gastroepiploic artery is a branch of the splenic artery and anastomoses with the right gastroepiploic artery.

questions.question_text: A patient with external hemorrhoids develops pain while passing stools. Which of the following nerves mediates this pain?
questions.explanation: External hemorrhoids are covered by the mucous membrane of the lower half of the anal canal or the skin and are innervated by the inferior rectal nerves, which are branches of the pudendal nerve. The lower half of the anal canal is sensitive to pain, temperature, touch, and pressure.

questions.question_text: The boundaries of the interconnection between the greater sac and lesser sac of peritoneum, known as the Foramen of Winslow, are all EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The superior boundary of the Foramen of Winslow is the caudate lobe of the liver. The anterior boundary is the free edge of the lesser omentum. The inferior boundary is the first part of the duodenum. The posterior boundary is the inferior vena cava and abdominal aorta.

questions.question_text: What is the number of layers in the greater omentum?
questions.explanation: The greater omentum is folded back on itself and is therefore made up of four layers of closely applied visceral peritoneum, separated by variable amounts of adipose tissue.

questions.question_text: All pass through the deep inguinal ring, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The deep inguinal ring transmits the spermatic cord in males and the round ligament of the uterus in females into the inguinal canal. The internal spermatic fascia is present in the spermatic cord. The ilioinguinal nerve passes through the superficial inguinal canal and not through the deep ring.

questions.question_text: All of the following arteries are branches of the coeliac trunk, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The branches of the coeliac trunk are the left gastric artery, splenic artery, and common hepatic artery. The right gastric artery is a branch of the common hepatic artery.

questions.question_text: Inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery is a branch of which of the following?
questions.explanation: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery is a branch of the superior mesenteric artery. Its anterior and posterior branches anastomose with branches of the superior pancreaticoduodenal artery. The source describes this as the communication between the arteries of the foregut and midgut.

questions.question_text: Portal vein is formed by union of which of the following veins?

options.text: Superior mesenteric vein and splenic vein
Superior mesenteric vein and inferior mesenteric vein
Inferior mesenteric vein and splenic vein
Inferior mesenteric vein and hepatic vein

questions.explanation: The portal vein is formed by the union of the superior mesenteric vein and splenic vein posterior to the neck of the pancreas. The inferior mesenteric vein drains into the splenic vein.

questions.question_text: Uvula vesicae seen in bladder is formed from the following structure?
questions.explanation: Uvula vesicae is a small elevation situated immediately behind the urethral orifice, produced by the underlying median lobe of the prostate. It enlarges with age due to enlargement of the median lobe and may inhibit complete bladder emptying.

questions.question_text: Facial nerve is a derivative of which of the following branchial arch?
questions.explanation: The facial nerve is a derivative of the second branchial arch. Muscles derived from it include the muscles of facial expression, stapedius, stylohyoid, and posterior belly of digastric.

questions.question_text: Which of the following nuclei belong to the general visceral afferent column?
questions.explanation: Visceral afferent fibres convey sensation from the alimentary tract, heart, vessels, and lungs by way of nerves IX and X. The general visceral afferent column is represented by part of the dorsal nucleus of the vagus nerve.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement regarding cell division is NOT TRUE?
questions.explanation: Mitosis is a nuclear division in which daughter cells receive the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell. It produces two genetically identical daughter cells and facilitates equal partitioning of replicated chromosomes.

questions.question_text: All the following features are seen in neurons from dorsal root ganglia, EXCEPT:

options.text: They are derived from neural crest cells

questions.explanation: Dorsal root ganglia consist of sensory neurons which are pseudounipolar and have no synaptic connections in the ganglion. They have a single axon that bifurcates into a central branch and a peripheral branch.

questions.question_text: Suprarenal gland gets its blood supply from all of the following arteries except:
questions.explanation: The suprarenal gland is supplied by suprarenal branches from the renal artery, inferior phrenic artery, and aorta. The source identifies the superior mesenteric artery as the exception.

questions.question_text: Internal anal sphincter is a part of:
questions.explanation: The involuntary internal anal sphincter is formed by thickening of the circular muscle layer of the upper end of the anal canal. It remains in a state of tonic contraction to maintain resting pressure and prevent leakage of fluid or flatus.

questions.question_text: During incision and drainage of ischiorectal abscess, which nerve is/are affected or injured?
questions.explanation: During dissection of the ischiorectal fossa, the inferior rectal, pudendal, posterior scrotal or labial nerves and vessels, along with perforating branches of S2–S3 and perineal branches of S4, may get damaged.

questions.question_text: Which structure(s) passes behind the inguinal ligament?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the femoral branch of the genitofemoral nerve, femoral vein, and psoas major as structures passing behind the inguinal ligament.

questions.question_text: Structure crossing dorsal surface of ischial spine are A/E:
questions.explanation: The PIN structures—pudendal nerve, internal pudendal vessels, and nerve to obturator internus—emerge through the greater sciatic foramen, cross the dorsal surface of the ischial spine, and enter the lesser sciatic foramen. The source identifies the obturator nerve as the exception.

questions.question_text: The muscles attached to perineal body are A/E:
questions.explanation: The source lists ten muscles converging and interlacing in the perineal body: the external anal sphincter, fibres of the longitudinal muscle coat of the anal canal, bulbospongiosus, superficial transverse perineal, deep transverse perineal, and levator ani muscles. It identifies ischiocavernosus as the exception.

questions.question_text: All are components of spermatic cord except:
questions.explanation: Poupart's ligament is also called the inguinal ligament and forms the base of the inguinal canal. The spermatic cord contains the ductus deferens, testicular and cremasteric arteries, artery of the ductus deferens, pampiniform plexus, lymph vessels, genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve, sympathetic fibres, and remains of the processus vaginalis.

questions.question_text: Shortest part of male urethra is:
questions.explanation: The membranous urethra is the shortest part, while the penile urethra is the longest. The prostatic urethra is the widest and most dilatable portion.

questions.question_text: Posterior communicating artery is a branch of:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the posterior communicating artery as a branch of the internal carotid artery.

questions.question_text: All are lateral branches of abdominal aorta, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The source lists the lateral branches of the abdominal aorta as the inferior phrenic, middle suprarenal, renal, and gonadal arteries. The inferior mesenteric artery is the exception.

questions.question_text: Arterial branches which supply the head and neck of the femur is/are:
questions.explanation: The proximal femur, including the head and neck, is supplied by the artery of ligamentum teres, the medial circumflex femoral artery, and the lateral circumflex femoral artery. The circumflex arteries arise from the profunda femoris artery according to the source.

questions.question_text: True about corpus callosum:

options.text: Unite far area of two sides of brain

questions.explanation: The source identifies all three statements as true: the corpus callosum connects the two cerebral hemispheres and connects corresponding areas between the two sides of the brain, including the frontal lobes.

questions.question_text: All are neural plate inducers except:
questions.explanation: The source identifies high BMP as the exception among the listed neural plate inducers.

questions.question_text: Structures derived from the neural crest are?
questions.explanation: The source identifies pia, dental papillae, and adrenal medulla as neural crest derivatives.

questions.question_text: Jelly formed around the heart tube during early development contributes to the formation of:
questions.explanation: The source identifies myocardium as the answer. It also states that dorsal mesocardium forms the transverse pericardial sinus, somatopleuric mesoderm forms parietal pericardium, and splanchnopleuric mesoderm forms myocardium and the conduction system of the heart. The source additionally states that cardiac jelly forms the endocardial cushion and myocardium.

questions.question_text: Primary and secondary palates are divided by:
questions.explanation: The incisive foramen is the dividing landmark between the primary and secondary palate.

questions.question_text: Obstruction of inferior vena cava presents:
questions.explanation: The source marks both A and B as correct: paraumbilical vein dilation and thoracoepigastric vein dilation. It explains that the thoracoepigastric vein drains to both the superior and inferior vena cava and is connected to the portal vein through the paraumbilical vein.

questions.question_text: The right suprarenal vein drains into the:
questions.explanation: The right suprarenal vein drains directly into the inferior vena cava. The left suprarenal vein usually drains into the left renal vein.

questions.question_text: True about the anatomy of great saphenous vein:

options.text: Starts as a continuation of medial marginal vein
Ends in femoral vein 2.5 cm below the inguinal ligament
There are 2–5 valves below the knee

questions.explanation: The source identifies the great saphenous vein as starting as a continuation of the medial marginal vein.

questions.question_text: Lymphatic drainage of cervix is to:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the iliac lymph nodes as the lymphatic drainage of the cervix.

questions.question_text: The thoracic duct crosses from the right to the left at the level of:
questions.explanation: The thoracic duct begins as a continuation of the upper end of the cisterna chyli near the lower border of T12 and enters the thorax through the aortic opening. It ascends through the posterior mediastinum and crosses from the right to the left at T5.

questions.question_text: Which of the following prevents hyperextension of thigh?
questions.explanation: Hip extension is limited by the iliofemoral ligament, which passes over the front of the hip joint and connects the ilium to the femur.

questions.question_text: Deltoid ligament is attached to all except:
questions.explanation: The deltoid ligament attaches to the medial malleolus and the navicular, talus, and calcaneus. Its tibionavicular part attaches to the spring ligament, and its tibiocalcaneal part attaches to the sustentaculum tali. The medial cuneiform is the exception.

questions.question_text: Ansa nephroni is lined by:
questions.explanation: The source identifies squamous epithelium as the lining of ansa nephroni.

questions.question_text: Auerbach's plexus is present in the:
questions.explanation: The source identifies Auerbach's plexus as present in the colon, esophagus, and stomach.

questions.question_text: Intercalated disc is present in:
questions.explanation: The source identifies cardiac muscle as the tissue containing intercalated discs.

questions.question_text: Which is true about synovial joint?

options.text: Stability is inversely proportional to mobility
Hyaline cartilage covers articular surface of all synovial joints
Metacarpophalangeal joint is a hinge joint
Cartilage usually divides the joint into two cavities

questions.explanation: The source identifies the inverse relationship between stability and mobility as the true statement about synovial joints.

questions.question_text: What is the uppermost structure in left lung hilum?
questions.explanation: The source states that in the left lung hilum, the pulmonary artery is the superior-most structure, followed by the principal bronchus and inferior pulmonary vein.

questions.question_text: Level of lower border of lung at mid axillary line is:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the 8th rib as the level of the lower border of the lung at the midaxillary line.

questions.question_text: True about anatomy of right ventricle:

options.text: Tricuspid valve and pulmonary valve share fibrous continuity
Crista supraventricularis separates tricuspid valve and pulmonary valve and apex is trabeculated

questions.explanation: The source marks all statements as correct. It also notes that the right ventricle is situated anteriorly and forms most of the anterior (sternocostal) surface of the heart.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not supplied by the anterior division of mandibular nerve (V3)?
questions.explanation: The source states that temporalis, masseter, and lateral pterygoid are supplied by the anterior division of the mandibular nerve, whereas medial pterygoid is supplied by the main trunk of the mandibular nerve.

questions.question_text: Nerve supply of stapedius is:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the seventh cranial nerve as the nerve supply of stapedius.

questions.question_text: Small muscles of hand are supplied by:
questions.explanation: All small muscles of the hand, including thenar, hypothenar, interossei and lumbricals, are supplied by the median and ulnar nerves, which originate from C5–C7 and C8–T1 nerve roots.

questions.question_text: Nerve damaged due to lunate dislocation in the carpal tunnel:
questions.explanation: The median nerve is the nerve affected in the carpal tunnel. The source identifies carpal tunnel syndrome as the most common cause of median nerve palsy in this region.

questions.question_text: Tibial nerve injury/palsy causes:

options.text: Dorsiflexion of foot at ankle joint
Plantar flexion of the foot at ankle joint
Loss of sensation of dorsum of foot
Paralysis of muscles of anterior compartment of leg

questions.explanation: The tibial nerve supplies the posterior compartment muscles that plantar-flex the ankle and foot. Injury causes loss of plantar flexion and a calcaneo-valgus attitude due to unopposed anterior compartment muscles, producing dorsiflexion and eversion.

questions.question_text: A patient presents with defective adduction of the hip joint and pain in the hip and knee joints. Which nerve is involved?
questions.explanation: The adductor muscles of the thigh are mainly supplied by the obturator nerve. Hip joint disease may cause referred pain in the knee and medial thigh because of their common nerve supply through the obturator nerve.

questions.question_text: All the following are characteristics of the oculomotor nerve except:

options.text: Enters orbit through the inferior orbital fissure

questions.explanation: The oculomotor nerve enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure. Its parasympathetic component controls the ciliary muscles and constrictor pupillae. It supplies all extraocular muscles except lateral rectus and superior oblique.

questions.question_text: Locking of knee joint can be caused by:
questions.explanation: The source gives the answer as both Osgood-Schlatter disease and a loose body. It also describes locking in association with meniscus tear, loose body due to osteochondral fracture and fractures of the tibial spine.

questions.question_text: Primordial germ cells are derived from:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the yolk sac as the origin of primordial germ cells. These cells migrate to the developing gonadal region.

questions.question_text: Ligamentum arteriosum is derived from:
questions.explanation: The ductus arteriosus represents the distal portion of the sixth left aortic arch. After birth, it normally constricts, closes and becomes the ligamentum arteriosum.

questions.question_text: Trigone of urinary bladder develops from:
questions.explanation: The trigone is formed by the part of the dorsal bladder wall marked off by the openings of the ureters and mesonephric ducts. Its lining is mesodermal in origin.

questions.question_text: Structure passes through upper triangular space:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the circumflex scapular vessels as contents of the space. The wording refers to the upper triangular space.

questions.question_text: Nerve roots involved in Erb's palsy:
questions.explanation: Erb-Duchenne palsy results from injury to the upper brachial plexus, involving excessive traction or tearing of the C5 and C6 roots.

questions.question_text: Structure passing deep to flexor retinaculum at wrist:
questions.explanation: The median nerve passes through the carpal tunnel deep to the flexor retinaculum, along with the flexor tendons of the thumb and fingers.

questions.question_text: Azygos vein drains into:
questions.explanation: The azygos vein arches forward above the root of the right lung and empties into the posterior surface of the superior vena cava.

questions.question_text: Arch of aorta begins and ends at which level:
questions.explanation: The arch of the aorta passes downward on the left side of the body of the fourth thoracic vertebra and becomes continuous with the descending aorta at its lower border.

questions.question_text: Azygos vein drains into:
questions.explanation: The azygos vein ends by joining the posterior aspect of the superior vena cava. It drains blood from the posterior walls of the thorax and abdomen.

questions.question_text: Vein used in bypass surgery:
questions.explanation: A portion of the great saphenous vein can be used as a graft to bypass an occluded coronary artery. The venous segment is reversed so its valves do not obstruct arterial flow.

questions.question_text: Superficial inguinal ring is a defect in the:
questions.explanation: The superficial inguinal ring is an opening in the aponeurosis of the external oblique muscle. The deep inguinal ring is an opening in the transversalis fascia.

questions.question_text: True about fallopian tubes are all except:

options.text: Isthmus is the narrower part of the tube that links to the uterus
Tubal ostium is the point where the tubal canal meets the peritoneal cavity
Müllerian ducts develop in females into the fallopian tubes

questions.explanation: The inner mucous membrane of the uterine tube is lined by ciliated columnar epithelium mixed with nonciliated secretory or peg cells. The isthmus is the narrowest part and lies just lateral to the uterus.

questions.question_text: Ovarian artery is a branch of:
questions.explanation: The ovarian artery arises from the abdominal part of the aorta at the level of the first lumbar vertebra.

questions.question_text: Parotid duct opens opposite to:
questions.explanation: The parotid duct opens opposite the upper second molar tooth.

questions.question_text: Largest cranial nerve is:
questions.explanation: The trigeminal nerve is the largest or thickest cranial nerve.

questions.question_text: Nucleus ambiguus is not associated with which cranial nerve:
questions.explanation: The nucleus ambiguus sends motor fibres through cranial nerves IX, X and the cranial portion of XI. It supplies muscles of the soft palate, pharynx, larynx and upper oesophagus.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not part of the ethmoid bone?
questions.explanation: The inferior turbinate is a separate bone. The middle and superior turbinates are parts of the ethmoidal labyrinth. The crista galli and uncinate process are also parts of the ethmoid bone.

questions.question_text: Meckel's cave is related to:
questions.explanation: The trigeminal ganglion, also called the Gasserian or semilunar ganglion, lies in a dural pouch called the cavum trigeminale or Meckel's cave.

questions.question_text: Medulla oblongata is derived from:
questions.explanation: The hindbrain develops from the rhombencephalon. Its myelencephalon gives rise to the medulla oblongata.

questions.question_text: Morula is how many celled?
questions.explanation: At about the 16-cell stage, blastomeres tightly align by compaction to form a compact ball of cells called the morula. The morula enters the uterine cavity four days after fertilization.

questions.question_text: Anterior interosseous nerve is a branch of:
questions.explanation: The anterior interosseous nerve is a branch of the median nerve. The anterior interosseous artery is a branch of the ulnar artery.

questions.question_text: Olecranon process of ulna helps in formation of:
questions.explanation: The inner surface of the olecranon process forms the trochlear notch for articulation with the trochlea of the humerus.

questions.question_text: True about cremasteric reflex?

options.text: Afferent: genital branch of genitofemoral nerve
Efferent: genital branch of genitofemoral nerve
Efferent: femoral branch of genitofemoral nerve

questions.explanation: The source identifies the efferent limb of the cremasteric reflex as the genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve.

questions.question_text: Longest spinous process is seen in:
questions.explanation: The seventh cervical vertebra is called vertebra prominens because it has the most prominent spinous process, which is not bifid.

questions.question_text: Malleus and incus are derived from:
questions.explanation: The first or mandibular arch contributes to the skeletal structures including the malleus and incus. It is also associated with the muscles of mastication and the trigeminal nerve.

questions.question_text: First rib is not related to:
questions.explanation: The source lists the sympathetic chain, first posterior intercostal vein, superior intercostal artery and first thoracic nerve as relations of the neck of the first rib. The scalenus anterior and suprapleural membrane are attached to the first rib.

questions.question_text: Optic cup is derived from:
questions.explanation: The optic cup is derived from neural ectoderm.

questions.question_text: Pyramidalis is supplied by:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the subcostal nerve as the nerve supply of pyramidalis.

questions.question_text: Excretory system of kidney is derived from:
questions.explanation: The metanephric mesoderm gives rise to the excretory unit or nephron, including the glomeruli, proximal convoluted tubule, loop of Henle and distal convoluted tubule. The ureteric bud forms the collecting system and ureter.

questions.question_text: Derivative of vitelline vein?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the inferior vena cava as a derivative of the vitelline vein.

questions.question_text: Sternochondral joint is:
questions.explanation: The source classifies costochondral joints and the first costosternal joint as primary cartilaginous joints.

questions.question_text: Sweat gland near the lid margins:
questions.explanation: Glands of Moll are apocrine sweat glands situated next to the eyelashes. Zeis and Meibomian glands are sebaceous glands, while Krause's glands are accessory lacrimal glands.

questions.question_text: Anterior lymphatics from the nose drain into:
questions.explanation: Submandibular lymph nodes receive lymph from the anterior part of the nasal cavity, among other structures. Their efferents drain into the upper and lower deep cervical nodes.

questions.question_text: Appendices epiploicae are seen in all parts of the large intestine except:
questions.explanation: Appendices epiploicae are small fat-filled peritoneal projections on the large intestine. The source states that they are absent over the appendix, caecum and rectum.

questions.question_text: Innervated structures of joints are all except:
questions.explanation: Articular cartilage has no nerve supply, no blood supply and no lymphatics. It also lacks a perichondrium and has no ability to repair or regenerate itself.

questions.question_text: Not true about inferior extensor retinaculum?

options.text: Superior slip attached to lower end of fibula
Inferior slip attached to deep fascia of sole

questions.explanation: The inferior extensor retinaculum is Y-shaped. Its stem attaches to the calcaneus; the upper band passes medially to the tibial malleolus, and the lower band blends with the plantar aponeurosis.

questions.question_text: Inferior rectal artery is a branch of:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the internal pudendal artery as the origin of the inferior rectal artery.

questions.question_text: Superficial epigastric artery is a branch of:
questions.explanation: The superficial epigastric artery is one of the superficial branches of the femoral artery.

questions.question_text: Inferior epigastric vein drains into:
questions.explanation: The inferior epigastric vein drains into the external iliac vein. The superior epigastric vein drains into the internal thoracic vein.

questions.question_text: Superior rectal vein drains into:
questions.explanation: The superior rectal vein drains into the inferior mesenteric vein. The inferior rectal vein drains into the internal pudendal vein.

questions.question_text: Killian's dehiscence is seen in:
questions.explanation: Killian's dehiscence is a potential gap between the thyropharyngeus and cricopharyngeus parts of the inferior constrictor muscle. It is a site where pharyngeal mucosa may herniate to form a pharyngeal pouch.

questions.question_text: Fossa incudis is related to:
questions.explanation: The fossa incudis contains the short process of the incus.

questions.question_text: Unpaired laryngeal cartilage?
questions.explanation: The unpaired laryngeal cartilages are thyroid, cricoid and epiglottis. Arytenoid, corniculate and cuneiform cartilages are paired.

questions.question_text: Which is the only nerve which exits the brainstem on the dorsal side?
questions.explanation: The trochlear nerve is the only cranial nerve to emerge from the dorsal aspect of the brain. It also undergoes complete internal decussation before emerging.

questions.question_text: Ureteric bud arises from:
questions.explanation: The ureteric bud arises from the mesonephric duct. The source describes the mesonephric and paramesonephric ducts as the two genital duct systems.

questions.question_text: Pisiform articulates with:
questions.explanation: The pisiform articulates with the triquetral.

questions.question_text: True about popliteus are all except:
questions.explanation: Popliteus unlocks the knee joint by laterally rotating the femur on the tibia before flexion. It is an accessory flexor of the knee, has an intracapsular origin and is supplied by the tibial nerve.

questions.question_text: 1st carpometacarpal joint is:
questions.explanation: The first carpometacarpal joint is a saddle joint.

questions.question_text: Most common location of accessory spleen?
questions.explanation: The most common site of an accessory spleen is the hilum of the spleen. Other sites listed include the tail of the pancreas and derivatives of the dorsal mesogastrium.

questions.question_text: Testis lies at deep inguinal ring up to:
questions.explanation: The testes reach the iliac fossa during the third month and lie at the site of the deep inguinal ring up to the seventh month of intrauterine life. They pass through the inguinal canal during the seventh month.

questions.question_text: Not true about development of ovary?

options.text: Sex cords are derived from coelomic epithelium
At birth ovary contains 2 million follicles

questions.explanation: The source states that primordial germ cells develop from endodermal cells of the hindgut, migrate to the developing ovary and give rise to oocytes. At birth, each ovary contains about two million primary follicles.

questions.question_text: Root value of supinator jerk:
questions.explanation: The source identifies C5 and C6 as the root values of the supinator jerk.

questions.question_text: True regarding semitendinosus?

options.text: Supplied by common peroneal part of sciatic nerve
Proximal and distal thin, middle fleshy

questions.explanation: Semitendinosus is a fusiform muscle with its main mass in the middle. It arises from the ischial tuberosity by a thin tendon and ends in a long tendon inserting on the medial surface of the proximal tibia. It is supplied by the tibial part of the sciatic nerve.

questions.question_text: True about blood supply of scaphoid?
questions.explanation: About 70–80% of the scaphoid's blood supply enters through its dorsal surface via dorsal branches of the radial artery. These vessels supply the proximal pole in a retrograde fashion.

questions.question_text: Which of the following dorsiflexes the foot?
questions.explanation: The tibialis anterior is responsible for dorsiflexion of the foot.

questions.question_text: Bare area of liver is related to:
questions.explanation: The bare area is a triangular region on the diaphragmatic surface of the liver that is not covered by peritoneum. The hepatic veins leave the liver in this area.

questions.question_text: Blood supply of putamen includes all except:
questions.explanation: The source lists lateral and medial striate branches and the anterior choroidal artery among the vessels supplying the putamen. The posterior communicating artery is the exception.

questions.question_text: True about notochord are all except:
questions.explanation: The notochord is formed by epiblast cells extending from the cranial end of the primitive streak. It defines the embryonic axis, acts as a primary inductor and persists partly as the nucleus pulposus.

questions.question_text: Length of Eustachian tube?
questions.explanation: The source gives the length of the Eustachian tube as 36 mm, reached by the age of seven years. The lateral third is bony and the medial two-thirds are fibrocartilaginous.

questions.question_text: Right coronary artery supplies all, except:
questions.explanation: The source states that the anterior two-thirds of the ventricular septum is supplied by the left coronary artery, while the posterior part is supplied by the right coronary artery.

questions.question_text: Bicipital aponeurosis lies over which structure in cubital fossa?
questions.explanation: The bicipital aponeurosis passes superficial to the brachial artery and median nerve. It provides limited protection to these structures during venipuncture.

questions.question_text: Structure over bicipital aponeurosis in cubital fossa?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the veins as structures lying superficial to the bicipital aponeurosis.

questions.question_text: 2nd part of duodenum is derived from:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the second part of the duodenum as having contributions from both the foregut and midgut.

questions.question_text: Artery piercing the oblique popliteal ligament of knee:
questions.explanation: The oblique popliteal ligament is an expansion from the tendon of semimembranosus. It is pierced by the middle genicular vessels and nerve and the terminal part of the posterior division of the obturator nerve.

questions.question_text: True about circumcaval ureter?

options.text: Ureter passes in front of IVC from lateral to medial

questions.explanation: Circumcaval or retrocaval ureter results from altered venous development and mostly involves the right ureter. The ureter passes behind the IVC and crosses in front of it from medial to lateral. Type 1 is more common.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a retroperitoneal structure?
questions.explanation: The ureter is a retroperitoneal structure.

questions.question_text: Falciform ligament contains:
questions.explanation: The falciform ligament contains the ligamentum teres, the remnant of the left umbilical vein, and paraumbilical veins.

questions.question_text: Parasympathetic supply to lacrimal glands is passed through:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the greater petrosal nerve as the pathway for parasympathetic supply to the lacrimal glands.

questions.question_text: Anterior part of interventricular septum is supplied by:
