questions.explanation: The anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum is supplied by the left coronary artery, while the posterior one-third is supplied by the right coronary artery.

questions.question_text: Part of colon with no mesentery?
questions.explanation: The ascending colon is secondarily retroperitoneal and does not have a mesentery. The transverse and sigmoid colon have mesocolons.

questions.question_text: True about right principal bronchus?
questions.explanation: Compared with the left principal bronchus, the right bronchus is shorter, wider and more vertical.

questions.question_text: Stroma of cornea develops from?
questions.explanation: The source identifies mesoderm as the origin of corneal stroma and surface ectoderm as the origin of corneal epithelium.

questions.question_text: Female genital tract develops from?
questions.explanation: The paramesonephric or Müllerian ducts develop into most of the female genital tract, including the uterine tubes, uterus and upper part of the vagina.

questions.question_text: Lateral dislocation of patella is prevented by?
questions.explanation: The vastus medialis, particularly its oblique fibres, helps prevent lateral displacement of the patella.

questions.question_text: Onodi cells are seen in?
questions.explanation: Onodi cells are posterior ethmoidal air cells. They may extend lateral and superior to the sphenoid sinus and lie close to the optic nerve.

questions.question_text: Which valve is present at opening of nasolacrimal duct?
questions.explanation: The nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus and is guarded by a mucosal fold called Hasner's valve. The Heister or spiral valve is found in the cystic duct.

questions.question_text: Thoracic duct is formed by?

options.text: Union of left subclavian and left internal jugular vein
Union of brachiocephalic vein and internal jugular vein
Continuation of upper end of cisterna chyli

questions.explanation: The thoracic duct begins as a continuation of the upper end of the cisterna chyli, usually near the lower border of T12.

questions.question_text: Thoracic duct opens into?
questions.explanation: The thoracic duct terminates at the left venous angle, where the left internal jugular and left subclavian veins unite.

questions.question_text: Submucosal plexus is?
questions.explanation: Meissner's plexus is the submucosal plexus. Auerbach's plexus is the myenteric plexus, located between the circular and longitudinal muscle layers.

questions.question_text: Femoral nerve supplies all except?
questions.explanation: Obturator externus is supplied by the obturator nerve. The femoral nerve supplies pectineus, sartorius and quadriceps femoris.

questions.question_text: Cribriform plate forms?
questions.explanation: The cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone forms part of the roof of the nasal cavity, including the olfactory region.

questions.question_text: Dental papilla gives rise to?
questions.explanation: The dental papilla gives rise to dentin-forming odontoblasts and the dental pulp. Enamel develops from the enamel organ.

questions.question_text: True about iliotibial tract all except?
questions.explanation: The iliotibial tract is a thickened lateral part of the fascia lata. It receives insertions from gluteus maximus and tensor fasciae latae and attaches to the lateral condyle of the tibia.

questions.question_text: False about sternocleidomastoid?

options.text: Motor supply by spinal accessory nerve
Tilts the head on opposite side

questions.explanation: Unilateral contraction of sternocleidomastoid tilts the head towards the same side and rotates the face towards the opposite side.

questions.question_text: False regarding trigone of bladder?

options.text: Internal urethral orifice lies at lateral angle of base

questions.explanation: The ureters open at the lateral angles of the trigone, while the internal urethral orifice lies at its apex.

questions.question_text: Boundaries of quadrilateral space include all except?
questions.explanation: The quadrangular space is bounded by teres minor superiorly, teres major inferiorly, long head of triceps medially and surgical neck of humerus laterally.

questions.question_text: Lamina papyracea is between?
questions.explanation: The lamina papyracea is the thin orbital plate of the ethmoid bone. It separates the ethmoidal air cells from the orbit.

questions.question_text: Glomus cells are derived from?
questions.explanation: Glomus cells are derived from neural crest cells, which originate from neuroectoderm.

questions.question_text: Axillary artery is divided into three parts by?
questions.explanation: Pectoralis minor divides the axillary artery into three parts: the first part medial to the muscle, the second part posterior to it and the third part lateral to it.

questions.question_text: Tongue muscle which is not developed from occipital myotome?
questions.explanation: Most tongue muscles develop from occipital myotomes and are supplied by the hypoglossal nerve. Palatoglossus is derived from the fourth pharyngeal arch and is supplied by the vagus nerve through the pharyngeal plexus.

questions.question_text: Korner's septum is seen in?
questions.explanation: Korner's septum is a persistent petrosquamous plate of bone within the mastoid process. It is surgically important because it can obscure the mastoid antrum.

questions.question_text: False about tibia-fibula is?

options.text: Nutrient artery of tibia is from posterior tibial artery
Nutrient artery of fibula is from peroneal artery
Proximal end of tibia is related to common peroneal nerve
Tibia is the most common site of osteomyelitis

questions.explanation: The common peroneal nerve winds around the neck of the fibula, not the proximal end of the tibia.

questions.question_text: Posterior wall of axilla is formed by?
questions.explanation: The posterior wall of the axilla is formed by subscapularis, teres major and latissimus dorsi. The source contains a duplicated option for pectoralis major.

questions.question_text: Intracapsular but extrasynovial is?
questions.explanation: The tendon of the long head of biceps passes within the capsule of the shoulder joint but remains extrasynovial.

questions.question_text: Posterior relation of hilum of lung?
questions.explanation: The vagus nerve passes posterior to the root of the lung, while the phrenic nerve passes anterior to it.

questions.question_text: What is true about chorda tympani?
questions.explanation: Chorda tympani carries preganglionic parasympathetic fibres to the submandibular ganglion and taste fibres from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue.

questions.question_text: Nephron is derived from?
questions.explanation: The metanephric mesoderm gives rise to the nephron, including the glomerulus, proximal convoluted tubule, loop of Henle and distal convoluted tubule. The ureteric bud forms the collecting system.

questions.question_text: Position of testis at 24–28 weeks of intrauterine life?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the deep inguinal ring as the position of the testis at 24–28 weeks of intrauterine life.

questions.question_text: Watershed zone of large intestine?
questions.explanation: The rectosigmoid junction, known as Sudeck's point, is a watershed area between the inferior mesenteric and internal iliac arterial territories. The splenic flexure is another watershed area.

questions.question_text: Skin over hypothenar eminence is supplied by?
questions.explanation: The skin over the hypothenar eminence is supplied by the palmar cutaneous branch of the ulnar nerve.

questions.question_text: Cremasteric artery is a branch of?
questions.explanation: The cremasteric artery is a branch of the inferior epigastric artery and supplies the cremaster muscle and coverings of the spermatic cord.

questions.question_text: Ligament extending from cervix and vagina to lateral pelvic wall?
questions.explanation: The transverse cervical or cardinal ligaments of Mackenrodt extend from the cervix and upper vagina to the lateral pelvic wall and provide support to the uterus.

questions.question_text: Epithelium of vagina arises from?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the upper two-thirds of the vagina as derived from the paramesonephric ducts and the lower third from the urogenital sinus. The question's single answer does not accurately describe the complete epithelial origin.

questions.question_text: Not related to hilum of right lung?
questions.explanation: The arch of the aorta is related to the root of the left lung, not the right lung.

questions.question_text: Anterior axillary fold is due to which muscle?
questions.explanation: The anterior axillary fold is formed by the lower border of pectoralis major. The posterior axillary fold is formed by latissimus dorsi and teres major.

questions.question_text: True about Scarpa's fascia?

options.text: Deep fascia of anterior abdominal wall

questions.explanation: Scarpa's fascia is the membranous layer of superficial fascia of the lower anterior abdominal wall. It contributes to the suspensory ligament of the penis.

questions.question_text: Skeletal derivative of first arch?
questions.explanation: The first pharyngeal arch contributes to the maxilla, mandible, malleus, incus and other skeletal structures.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is derived from first arch?
questions.explanation: Both maxillary and mandibular processes develop from the first pharyngeal arch. The frontonasal process develops independently from mesenchyme overlying the developing brain.

questions.question_text: Woodruff's area is located at?

options.text: Posteroinferior part of lateral nasal wall

questions.explanation: Woodruff's area is located on the posteroinferior lateral wall of the nasal cavity, beneath the posterior end of the inferior turbinate.

questions.question_text: Scutum is present in middle ear?
questions.explanation: The scutum is a sharp bony projection on the lateral wall of the epitympanic recess of the middle ear.

questions.question_text: Ovarian fossa is formed by all except?
questions.explanation: The ovarian fossa is bounded anteriorly by the obliterated umbilical artery and posteriorly by the ureter and internal iliac artery. The round ligament of the ovary is not a boundary.

questions.question_text: Appendices epiploicae is a feature of?
questions.explanation: Appendices epiploicae are fat-filled peritoneal pouches characteristic of the large intestine. They are absent from the appendix, caecum and rectum.

questions.question_text: Nerve entering the inguinal canal through deep inguinal ring?
questions.explanation: The genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve enters the inguinal canal through the deep inguinal ring. The ilioinguinal nerve enters the canal through the abdominal wall between the internal and external oblique muscles.

questions.question_text: How many lactiferous ducts open in nipple?
questions.explanation: The source states that approximately 15–20 lactiferous ducts open separately on the nipple.

questions.question_text: Optic cup gives rise to?
questions.explanation: The optic cup develops into the retina, including its neural and pigmented layers. The lens develops from surface ectoderm.

questions.question_text: Not a part of bony labyrinth?
questions.explanation: The bony labyrinth consists of the cochlea, vestibule and semicircular canals. The utricle is part of the membranous labyrinth.

questions.question_text: Lymphatic drainage of thyroid gland is mainly?
questions.explanation: Thyroid lymph drains mainly to the deep cervical lymph nodes, directly or through prelaryngeal, pretracheal and paratracheal nodes.

questions.question_text: Hunter's canal is seen in?
questions.explanation: Hunter's canal, also called the adductor canal, is located in the middle third of the thigh.

questions.question_text: Organ of Corti is situated in?
questions.explanation: The organ of Corti rests on the basilar membrane within the cochlear duct.

questions.question_text: Initially, renal arteries are branches of?
questions.explanation: During early development, when the kidneys are in the pelvis, their arteries arise from the common iliac arteries. As the kidneys ascend, they acquire new arterial branches from the aorta.

questions.question_text: In a neonate, kidney is supplied by?
questions.explanation: After renal ascent, the definitive renal arteries arise from the abdominal aorta. The source identifies the aorta as the arterial supply in the neonate.

questions.question_text: Hassall's corpuscles are found in?
questions.explanation: Hassall's corpuscles are concentric, eosinophilic structures found in the medulla of the thymus.

questions.question_text: Bronchopulmonary segments in right and left lungs respectively?
questions.explanation: The source gives 10 bronchopulmonary segments in each lung. Some anatomical descriptions count fewer segments in the left lung because of fused or variable segments.

questions.question_text: Vidian nerve is formed by union of?

options.text: Superficial petrosal nerve and deep petrosal nerve
Greater petrosal nerve and superficial petrosal nerve
Greater petrosal nerve and deep petrosal nerve
Greater petrosal nerve and external petrosal nerve

questions.explanation: The greater petrosal nerve joins the deep petrosal nerve to form the nerve of the pterygoid canal, also called the Vidian nerve.

questions.question_text: Structure related to deltopectoral groove?
questions.explanation: The cephalic vein runs in the deltopectoral groove between the deltoid and pectoralis major muscles.

questions.question_text: 3rd and 4th lumbricals (lateral two lumbricals) of foot are supplied by?
questions.explanation: The lateral plantar nerve supplies the second, third and fourth lumbricals of the foot. The medial plantar nerve supplies the first lumbrical.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a derivative of paramesonephric duct in males?
questions.explanation: The paramesonephric duct remnants in males include the appendix of the testis and the prostatic utricle.

questions.question_text: Floor of 4th ventricle has?
questions.explanation: The floor of the fourth ventricle, or rhomboid fossa, contains the vagal triangle overlying the dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus.

questions.question_text: Breast is a?
questions.explanation: The breast is a modified sweat gland. Its secretory activity has both merocrine and apocrine features.

questions.question_text: Nerve which loops around submandibular duct?
questions.explanation: The lingual nerve loops around the submandibular duct, passing from lateral to medial beneath it before ascending towards the tongue.

questions.question_text: At the level of arch of aorta, the relationship of left vagus nerve and left phrenic nerve?

options.text: Phrenic nerve anterior, vagus nerve posterior
Phrenic nerve posterior, vagus nerve anterior

questions.explanation: The left phrenic nerve passes anterior to the root of the lung and the left vagus nerve passes posterior to it. At the arch of the aorta, the phrenic nerve is anterior to the vagus nerve.

questions.question_text: Pharyngeal muscles are derived from which pharyngeal arch?
questions.explanation: The source gives the third pharyngeal arch as the answer. However, pharyngeal muscles have contributions from several arches: the third arch gives rise to stylopharyngeus, while most other pharyngeal muscles arise from the fourth and sixth arches.

questions.question_text: Styloid process is derived from?
questions.explanation: The styloid process develops from Reichert's cartilage of the second pharyngeal arch.

questions.question_text: Common interosseous artery is a branch of?
questions.explanation: The common interosseous artery is a branch of the ulnar artery and divides into anterior and posterior interosseous arteries.

questions.question_text: Haller cells are seen in?
questions.explanation: Haller cells are ethmoidal air cells that extend into the orbital floor, near the maxillary sinus ostium.

questions.question_text: True about clavicle?
questions.explanation: The clavicle has no medullary cavity. It is the first bone to begin ossification, lies horizontally and is the most commonly fractured long bone.

questions.question_text: Secondary ossification center for lower end of femur?
questions.explanation: The secondary ossification center at the lower end of the femur appears around the ninth month of intrauterine life and is therefore present at birth.

questions.question_text: All are branches of lumbar plexus except?
questions.explanation: The subcostal nerve is the anterior ramus of T12 and is not a branch of the lumbar plexus. The iliohypogastric, ilioinguinal and obturator nerves are lumbar plexus branches.

questions.question_text: External oblique forms all except?
questions.explanation: The conjoint tendon is formed by the aponeuroses of internal oblique and transversus abdominis. The inguinal, lacunar and pectineal ligaments are associated with the external oblique aponeurosis.

questions.question_text: Posterior to transverse pericardial sinus?
questions.explanation: The transverse pericardial sinus lies behind the ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk and in front of the superior vena cava.

questions.question_text: Medulla is supplied by all except?
questions.explanation: The medulla receives blood from branches of the vertebral arteries, anterior spinal artery and posterior inferior cerebellar arteries. The posterior cerebral artery is not a principal supplier.

questions.question_text: Articular surface of the sacrum extends up to how many vertebrae in males?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the sacral auricular articular surface as extending across approximately three to three-and-a-half vertebral levels in males.

questions.question_text: Lower limit of sacroiliac joint lies up to which level in females?
questions.explanation: The source gives the lower limit of the sacroiliac joint in females as approximately two to two-and-a-half vertebral levels.

questions.question_text: Fibrin is degraded by?
questions.explanation: Plasmin breaks down fibrin into fibrin degradation products. It is formed from plasminogen through the action of plasminogen activators.

questions.question_text: Which is not an extrapyramidal tract?
questions.explanation: The corticospinal tract is the principal pyramidal tract. Reticulospinal, rubrospinal and tectospinal tracts are extrapyramidal pathways.

questions.question_text: Sensory perception involves Brodmann's area?
questions.explanation: Brodmann areas 3, 1 and 2 form the primary somatosensory cortex in the postcentral gyrus of the parietal lobe.

questions.question_text: Gastric acid secretion is stimulated by all except?
questions.explanation: Gastric distension, gastrin and the sight or smell of food stimulate gastric acid secretion. Somatostatin inhibits gastric acid secretion.

questions.question_text: Hangman's fracture is the fracture involving which cervical vertebra?
questions.explanation: Hangman's fracture is a bilateral fracture through the pars interarticularis of the axis (C2), often associated with traumatic displacement of C2 over C3.

questions.question_text: Which of the following does not directly drain into right atrium?
questions.explanation: The great cardiac vein drains into the coronary sinus, which then opens into the right atrium. Anterior cardiac veins and venae cordis minimae drain directly into the heart chambers.

questions.question_text: Gastrosplenic ligament contains?
questions.explanation: The gastrosplenic ligament contains the short gastric and left gastro-omental vessels.

questions.question_text: Where is the Cave of Retzius present?

options.text: Between the cervix and the rectum

questions.explanation: The space of Retzius is a potential retropubic space situated anterior to the urinary bladder.

questions.question_text: Incudomalleolar joint is a?
questions.explanation: The incudomalleolar joint is a saddle-type synovial joint.

questions.question_text: Right border of heart is formed by?
questions.explanation: The right border of the heart is formed by the right atrium.

questions.question_text: Which of the following leaves the pelvis?
questions.explanation: The sciatic nerve leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen, usually below piriformis, and enters the gluteal region.

questions.question_text: Which structure develops from the Müllerian duct in males?
questions.explanation: The prostatic utricle is a remnant of the paramesonephric (Müllerian) duct in males.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a tributary of the coronary sinus?
questions.explanation: The great cardiac vein is a major tributary of the coronary sinus.

questions.question_text: Wrist drop is due to injury to?
questions.explanation: Radial nerve injury can paralyse the wrist extensors, producing wrist drop.

questions.question_text: All are true about the short saphenous vein except?

options.text: Runs on the lateral side of the leg
Achilles tendon is medial to the vein

questions.explanation: The short saphenous vein ascends in the posterior aspect of the leg, behind the lateral malleolus, accompanied by the sural nerve.

questions.question_text: What is the nerve supply of the cremasteric muscle?
questions.explanation: The cremaster muscle is supplied by the genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve.

questions.question_text: Trigone of the urinary bladder is derived from?
questions.explanation: The bladder trigone develops from the incorporated caudal ends of the mesonephric ducts.

questions.question_text: Bartholin gland is situated in?
questions.explanation: The greater vestibular (Bartholin) glands are located in the superficial perineal pouch.

questions.question_text: Vasa vasorum of the ascending aorta arises from?
questions.explanation: The source identifies coronary arteries as the supply of vasa vasorum of the ascending aorta; the left coronary artery is the keyed option.

questions.question_text: Middle meningeal artery passes through?
questions.explanation: The middle meningeal artery enters the cranial cavity through the foramen spinosum.

questions.question_text: Which structure lies outside the femoral sheath?
questions.explanation: The femoral nerve lies outside the femoral sheath, lateral to it. The femoral artery and vein are contained within the sheath.

questions.question_text: Lateral border of the ischiorectal fossa is formed by?
questions.explanation: The lateral wall of the ischioanal fossa is formed by the obturator internus muscle and its fascia, with the ischial tuberosity.

questions.question_text: Superior gluteal nerve does not supply?
questions.explanation: Gluteus maximus is supplied by the inferior gluteal nerve. The superior gluteal nerve supplies gluteus medius, gluteus minimus and tensor fasciae latae.

questions.question_text: Which muscle of the arm has an additional supinator action?
questions.explanation: The biceps brachii is a powerful supinator of the forearm, particularly when the elbow is flexed.

questions.question_text: Lymphatic drainage of the ovary is primarily to which lymph nodes?
questions.explanation: Ovarian lymphatics follow the ovarian vessels to the para-aortic (lumbar) lymph nodes.

questions.question_text: Anal valve is found in which part of the anal canal?
questions.explanation: Anal valves are mucosal folds connecting the lower ends of the anal columns in the upper part of the anal canal.

questions.question_text: Which muscle is inserted into the floor of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus?
questions.explanation: Latissimus dorsi inserts into the floor of the intertubercular sulcus. Pectoralis major inserts on the lateral lip.

questions.question_text: Ventral pancreatic duct gives rise to?
questions.explanation: The ventral pancreatic bud forms the inferior part of the pancreatic head, including the uncinate process.

questions.question_text: All are derived from neural crest except?
questions.explanation: Retinal pigment epithelium develops from the neuroectoderm of the optic cup, not from neural crest.

questions.question_text: True about the atrioventricular groove are all except?

options.text: Contains left anterior descending coronary artery
Contains circumflex branch of left coronary artery

questions.explanation: The left anterior descending artery runs in the anterior interventricular groove, not the atrioventricular groove.

questions.question_text: Intercostal nerve is a branch of?

options.text: Dorsal rami of thoracic spinal nerves
Ventral rami of thoracic spinal nerves
Ventral rami of cervical spinal nerves

questions.explanation: Intercostal nerves are the ventral rami of thoracic spinal nerves T1–T11. The T12 ventral ramus is the subcostal nerve.

questions.question_text: All are true about the first part of the duodenum except?
questions.explanation: The proximal duodenum develops from the foregut and is supplied mainly by the coeliac trunk through the superior pancreaticoduodenal artery.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a derivative of the ventral mesogastrium?
questions.explanation: The ventral mesogastrium gives rise to the lesser omentum and falciform ligament.

questions.question_text: Number of vertebrae is usually constant in?
questions.explanation: The cervical region is the most constant region of the vertebral column in terms of vertebral number.

questions.question_text: Which of the following structures is seen in the cavernous sinus?
questions.explanation: The internal carotid artery passes through the cavernous sinus. The maxillary and mandibular divisions of the trigeminal nerve do not pass through it.

questions.question_text: Valve of Heister is seen in?
questions.explanation: The spiral folds of the mucous membrane in the cystic duct are known as the valve of Heister.

questions.question_text: Eustachian tube opens into the middle ear in which wall?
questions.explanation: The pharyngotympanic (Eustachian) tube opens into the anterior wall of the middle ear.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is related to the mediastinal part of the right lung?
questions.explanation: The mediastinal surface of the right lung has a groove for the superior vena cava.

questions.question_text: Esophagus is present in all except?
questions.explanation: The esophagus descends through the superior and posterior mediastina and has no relation to the anterior mediastinum.

questions.question_text: Which is a skeletal derivative of the second pharyngeal arch?
questions.explanation: The stapes is derived from the second pharyngeal arch. The malleus and incus are derived from the first arch.

questions.question_text: Clavipectoral fascia is derived from which ligament?
questions.explanation: The costocoracoid membrane is the thickened superior part of the clavipectoral fascia.

questions.question_text: What is the nerve supply of the larynx above the level of the vocal cords?
questions.explanation: Sensory supply above the vocal cords is provided by the internal laryngeal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve.

questions.question_text: What is the root value of the thoracodorsal nerve?
questions.explanation: The thoracodorsal nerve arises from the posterior cord of the brachial plexus and carries fibres from C6, C7 and C8.

questions.question_text: Length of the posterior vaginal wall is?
questions.explanation: The posterior vaginal wall is approximately 10 cm long, while the anterior wall is approximately 8 cm long.

questions.question_text: Which lymph nodes drain the upper vagina and cervix?
questions.explanation: The upper third of the vagina and cervix drain mainly to the external iliac nodes, with cervical drainage also reaching internal iliac and sacral nodes.

questions.question_text: Posterior surface of the heart is formed mainly by?
questions.explanation: The base or posterior surface of the heart is formed mainly by the left atrium and partly by the right atrium.

questions.question_text: Largest branch of the brachial plexus is?
questions.explanation: The radial nerve is the largest branch of the brachial plexus and is the continuation of its posterior cord.

questions.question_text: Which muscle of the larynx is not supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve?
questions.explanation: All intrinsic muscles of the larynx are supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve except cricothyroid, which is supplied by the external laryngeal nerve.

questions.question_text: All are infraclavicular branches of the brachial plexus except?
questions.explanation: The long thoracic nerve arises from the roots of the brachial plexus and is a supraclavicular branch.

questions.question_text: A surgeon removes a part of the liver to the left of the falciform ligament. Which segments of the liver are removed?
questions.explanation: The left anatomical lobe, to the left of the falciform ligament, corresponds mainly to Couinaud segments II and III.

questions.question_text: Esophagus is present in which mediastinum?
questions.explanation: The thoracic esophagus descends through the superior and posterior mediastina.

questions.question_text: Which structure lies posterior to the sternum?
questions.explanation: The right ventricle forms most of the anterior (sternocostal) surface of the heart and lies directly behind the sternum.

questions.question_text: Location of the testis is higher on which side?

options.text: May be on right or left side

questions.explanation: The source identifies the right testis as being positioned higher than the left testis.

questions.question_text: Distal end of the humerus develops from how many ossification centres?
questions.explanation: The distal end of the humerus has four secondary ossification centres: capitulum with lateral trochlear flange, medial trochlear flange, lateral epicondyle and medial epicondyle.

questions.question_text: Clavipectoral fascia is pierced by all except?
questions.explanation: The clavipectoral fascia is pierced by the cephalic vein, thoracoacromial vessels, lateral pectoral nerve and lymphatics. The medial pectoral nerve is not listed among these structures.

questions.question_text: Stomach is supplied by?
questions.explanation: The stomach receives arterial supply through branches of the coeliac trunk, including branches of the splenic and common hepatic arteries such as the gastroduodenal artery.

questions.question_text: Which muscle plays a role in winking?
questions.explanation: Orbicularis oculi closes the eyelids and is responsible for blinking and winking.

questions.question_text: Which muscle is attached to the lateral surface of the greater trochanter?
questions.explanation: Gluteus medius inserts onto the lateral surface of the greater trochanter.

questions.question_text: Support of the prostate is provided by?
questions.explanation: The pubococcygeus fibres surround the prostate and form the levator prostatae, helping support it.

questions.question_text: Which type of collagen is found in hyaline cartilage?
questions.explanation: Type II collagen is the predominant collagen in hyaline cartilage.

questions.question_text: Galen's anastomosis is between?

options.text: Recurrent laryngeal nerve and external laryngeal nerve
Recurrent laryngeal nerve and internal laryngeal nerve
Internal laryngeal nerve and external laryngeal nerve

questions.explanation: Galen's anastomosis connects the recurrent laryngeal nerve with the internal laryngeal nerve.

questions.question_text: Radial bursa is the synovial sheath covering the tendon of?
questions.explanation: The radial bursa surrounds the tendon of flexor pollicis longus.

questions.question_text: Which muscle will be paralysed when the radial nerve is injured just below the spiral groove?
questions.explanation: The source identifies extensor carpi radialis longus as affected by a lesion just below the spiral groove. The exact level of radial nerve injury and branching can affect which muscles are spared.

questions.question_text: Which are the segments of the upper lobe of the right lung?
questions.explanation: The right upper lobe has three bronchopulmonary segments: apical, posterior and anterior.

questions.question_text: Centroacinar cells are present in?
questions.explanation: Centroacinar cells are characteristic of the exocrine pancreas and represent the beginning of the intercalated ducts.

questions.question_text: Billroth's cords are present in which part of the spleen?
questions.explanation: The splenic cords of Billroth are found in the red pulp of the spleen.

questions.question_text: B-cells are dispersed in which part of the spleen?
questions.explanation: B lymphocytes are present in the white pulp, particularly within the lymphoid follicles.

questions.question_text: Neurovascular bundle of the anterior compartment of the leg passes between the tendons of?

options.text: Extensor hallucis longus and extensor digitorum longus
Extensor digitorum longus and peroneus tertius
Tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus

questions.explanation: The anterior tibial vessels and deep fibular nerve pass between the tendons of extensor hallucis longus and extensor digitorum longus near the ankle.

questions.question_text: Which is a true statement about the great saphenous vein?

options.text: It begins at the lateral end of the dorsal venous arch
It runs anterior to the medial malleolus
It is accompanied by the sural nerve
It terminates into the popliteal vein

questions.explanation: The great saphenous vein passes anterior to the medial malleolus and terminates in the femoral vein.

questions.question_text: In the arm, the ulnar nerve gives muscular branches to which muscles?
questions.explanation: The ulnar nerve supplies flexor carpi ulnaris and the medial half of flexor digitorum profundus.

questions.question_text: Vertebral arteries of both sides unite to form?
questions.explanation: The two vertebral arteries unite at the lower border of the pons to form the basilar artery.

questions.question_text: Follicles are present in which part of lymph nodes?
questions.explanation: Lymphoid follicles are found in the cortex of lymph nodes.

questions.question_text: Remnant of the notochord is?
questions.explanation: The nucleus pulposus of the intervertebral disc is derived from the notochord.

questions.question_text: Which structure passes deep to the flexor retinaculum?
questions.explanation: The posterior tibial artery passes deep to the flexor retinaculum behind the medial malleolus.

questions.question_text: Which muscles are known as triceps surae?
questions.explanation: The gastrocnemius and soleus muscles together form the triceps surae.

questions.question_text: All are true regarding axillary lymph nodes except?

options.text: Posterior group lies along subscapular vessels
Lateral group lies along lateral thoracic vessels
Apical group lies along axillary vessels
Apical group is the terminal lymph node group

questions.explanation: The lateral group lies along the upper part of the humerus, medial to the axillary vein. The anterior (pectoral) group lies along the lateral thoracic vessels.

questions.question_text: Thoracic duct does not drain which region?
questions.explanation: The thoracic duct drains the entire body below the diaphragm and the left upper quadrant. The right upper quadrant drains into the right lymphatic duct.

questions.question_text: Which statement is not true about the right bronchus?

options.text: In the line of the trachea

questions.explanation: The right main bronchus is shorter, wider and more vertical than the left main bronchus.

questions.question_text: All are true about the mammary gland except?

options.text: It is a modified sweat gland
It extends from the 2nd to the 6th rib vertically
It is supplied by the internal mammary artery
The nipple is supplied by the 6th intercostal nerve

questions.explanation: The nipple is mainly supplied by the fourth intercostal nerve, not the sixth.

questions.question_text: The nerve supply of the nail bed of the index finger is?
questions.explanation: The nail bed of the index finger is supplied by digital branches of the median nerve.

questions.question_text: The blood supply to the femoral head is mostly by?
questions.explanation: The major blood supply to the femoral head is through retinacular branches, mainly from the medial circumflex femoral artery, a branch of the profunda femoris.

questions.question_text: All pass through the jugular foramen except?
questions.explanation: The mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve passes through the foramen ovale, not the jugular foramen.

questions.question_text: Boundaries of the anatomical snuffbox are all except?
questions.explanation: The anatomical snuffbox is bounded by abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis laterally, and extensor pollicis longus medially.

questions.question_text: Medial boundary of the cubital fossa is formed by?
questions.explanation: The medial boundary of the cubital fossa is formed by the lateral border of pronator teres.

questions.question_text: Superficial perineal space contains?
questions.explanation: The superficial perineal pouch contains the ischiocavernosus, bulbospongiosus and superficial transverse perineal muscles.

questions.question_text: Caudate lobe of the liver is which segment?
questions.explanation: The caudate lobe corresponds to Couinaud segment I.

questions.question_text: Spinal cord develops from?
questions.explanation: The spinal cord develops from the caudal part of the neural tube, which forms through neurulation.

questions.question_text: Hyoid lies at the level of?
questions.explanation: The hyoid bone lies approximately at the level of the third cervical vertebra.

questions.question_text: Which of the following muscles is not in the pectoral region?
questions.explanation: Infraspinatus is a muscle of the scapular region and rotator cuff, not the pectoral region.

questions.question_text: True about linea aspera?
questions.explanation: The upper part of the linea aspera continues proximally as the gluteal tuberosity laterally.

questions.question_text: Hunterian perforators are seen in?
questions.explanation: The Hunterian perforator is associated with the adductor canal region in the middle of the thigh.

questions.question_text: Internal spermatic fascia is derived from?
questions.explanation: The internal spermatic fascia is derived from the transversalis fascia as the spermatic cord passes through the deep inguinal ring.

questions.question_text: Portal vein supplies?
questions.explanation: The portal vein carries nutrient-rich blood from the gastrointestinal tract and spleen to the liver, providing most of its blood flow.

questions.question_text: Collecting part of kidney develops from?
questions.explanation: The ureteric bud forms the collecting system of the kidney, including the renal pelvis, calyces, collecting ducts and ureter.

questions.question_text: Nerve running along with profunda brachii artery in the spiral groove?
questions.explanation: The radial nerve accompanies the profunda brachii artery in the radial (spiral) groove of the humerus.

questions.question_text: In which of the following vessels is the transverse mesocolon seen?
questions.explanation: The transverse mesocolon contains the middle colic vessels.

questions.question_text: Main blood supply to the head and neck of femur comes from?
questions.explanation: The medial circumflex femoral artery gives retinacular and epiphyseal branches that provide most of the blood supply to the femoral head and neck.

questions.question_text: Pubic symphysis is which type of joint?
questions.explanation: The pubic symphysis is a secondary cartilaginous joint containing fibrocartilage.

questions.question_text: At which level do somites initially form?
questions.explanation: The first pair of somites forms in the neck region, posterior to the cranial end of the notochord.

questions.question_text: Double inferior vena cava is formed due to?

options.text: Persistence of both supracardinal and subcardinal veins

questions.explanation: The source attributes double inferior vena cava to persistence of both supracardinal and subcardinal veins below the kidneys.

questions.question_text: All of the following muscles have dual nerve supply except?
questions.explanation: Pronator teres is supplied by the median nerve. The other listed muscles have dual nerve contributions.

questions.question_text: A person had an injury to the right upper limb. He is not able to extend fingers but is able to extend the wrist and elbow. Which nerve is injured?
questions.explanation: Posterior interosseous nerve injury causes loss of finger and thumb extension while wrist extension is relatively preserved because extensor carpi radialis longus is spared. It is a motor nerve, so sensory loss is absent.

questions.question_text: The retina is an outgrowth of the?
questions.explanation: The optic vesicle develops as an outgrowth of the diencephalon and forms the optic cup, which gives rise to the retina.

questions.question_text: All are contents of the occipital triangle except?
questions.explanation: The suprascapular nerve passes toward the supraspinous fossa and is not a content of the occipital triangle.

questions.question_text: Contents of the midpalmar space are all except?

options.text: Flexor digitorum profundus tendon of third finger
Flexor digitorum profundus tendon of fourth finger

questions.explanation: The first lumbrical is associated with the thenar space, whereas the midpalmar space contains the second, third and fourth lumbricals and the flexor tendons of the medial fingers.

questions.question_text: Axillary nerve is accompanied by which artery?
questions.explanation: The axillary nerve accompanies the posterior circumflex humeral artery through the quadrangular space.

questions.question_text: The roof of the olfactory region is formed by?
questions.explanation: The cribriform plate of the ethmoid forms the roof of the olfactory region of the nasal cavity.

questions.question_text: Superior pancreaticoduodenal artery is a branch of?
questions.explanation: The superior pancreaticoduodenal artery arises from the gastroduodenal artery.

questions.question_text: Helicine arteries are branches of?
questions.explanation: Helicine arteries arise from the deep artery of the penis and supply the erectile tissue of the corpora cavernosa.

questions.question_text: The superficial external pudendal artery is a branch of?
questions.explanation: The superficial external pudendal artery is one of the superficial branches of the femoral artery.

questions.question_text: Nerve supply to the muscles of the flexor compartment of the arm?
questions.explanation: The musculocutaneous nerve supplies the coracobrachialis, biceps brachii and brachialis muscles in the anterior compartment of the arm.

questions.question_text: Tributaries of the cavernous sinus are all except?
questions.explanation: The cavernous sinus receives the inferior cerebral vein, central retinal vein and sphenoparietal sinus. The superior cerebral veins mainly drain into the superior sagittal sinus.

questions.question_text: Line from midinguinal point to adductor tubercle represents?
questions.explanation: The femoral artery is surface-marked by the upper two-thirds of a line joining the midinguinal point to the adductor tubercle.

questions.question_text: Pineal gland forms?
questions.explanation: The pineal body is a component of the posterior wall of the third ventricle.

questions.question_text: Epithelial lining of urinary bladder?
questions.explanation: The urinary bladder is lined by transitional epithelium, also known as urothelium.

questions.question_text: Chorda tympani is a part of?
questions.explanation: The chorda tympani, a branch of the facial nerve, traverses the middle ear cavity.

questions.question_text: Greater petrosal nerve is formed from?
questions.explanation: The greater petrosal nerve arises from the facial nerve at the geniculate ganglion and carries preganglionic parasympathetic fibres.

questions.question_text: Base of the heart is formed by?
questions.explanation: The base or posterior surface of the heart is formed mainly by the left atrium and partly by the right atrium.

questions.question_text: True about cardiac muscle is?
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle cells are branched and striated, usually with one centrally located nucleus. They contain intercalated discs with gap junctions.

questions.question_text: Muscle causing supination of forearm?
questions.explanation: Biceps brachii is a powerful supinator of the forearm, especially when the elbow is flexed.

questions.question_text: Third extensor compartment of wrist contains the tendon of?
questions.explanation: The third extensor compartment contains the tendon of extensor pollicis longus.

questions.question_text: Ligament supporting the talus is?
questions.explanation: The spring ligament, or plantar calcaneonavicular ligament, supports the head of the talus and helps maintain the medial longitudinal arch.

questions.question_text: Upper two posterior intercostal arteries arise from?
questions.explanation: The first and second posterior intercostal arteries arise from the supreme intercostal artery, which is a branch of the costocervical trunk. The source uses the term superior intercostal artery.

questions.question_text: Which thalamic nuclei connect with the neocortex?
questions.explanation: The listed thalamic nuclei have connections with cortical regions, although their specific cortical targets and functions differ.

questions.question_text: Stapedius nerve is a branch of?
questions.explanation: The nerve to stapedius arises from the facial nerve within the facial canal.

questions.question_text: Deep injury of the neck always involves?
questions.explanation: A penetrating injury that reaches the deeper structures of the neck must pass through the platysma.

questions.question_text: Glomus cells are found in?
questions.explanation: Glomus cells are chemoreceptor cells found in structures such as the carotid and aortic bodies.

questions.question_text: Most dependent part of the abdomen in standing position is?
questions.explanation: The rectouterine pouch, also called the pouch of Douglas, is the most dependent part of the female peritoneal cavity in the erect position. Options B and C describe the same pouch.

questions.question_text: Carina is situated at which level?
questions.explanation: The trachea bifurcates at the carina near the T4–T5 intervertebral disc, approximately at the sternal angle.

questions.question_text: Pelvic pain is mediated by?
questions.explanation: Visceral afferent fibres from pelvic organs travel with autonomic pathways. The exact route depends on the organ's relationship to the pelvic pain line.

questions.question_text: Posterior relation of the neck of pancreas?
questions.explanation: The neck of the pancreas lies anterior to the formation of the portal vein, which is formed behind it by the union of the superior mesenteric and splenic veins.

questions.question_text: Protrusion of tongue is not possible in damage of?
questions.explanation: Genioglossus is the main protruder of the tongue. Bilateral paralysis causes inability to protrude the tongue.

questions.question_text: Terminal branches of the internal carotid artery are all except?
questions.explanation: The internal carotid artery terminates by dividing into the anterior and middle cerebral arteries. The cavernous artery is a branch of its cavernous segment, not a terminal branch.

questions.question_text: Little's area is?
questions.explanation: Little's area, or Kiesselbach's plexus, is located in the anteroinferior part of the nasal septum and is a common site of epistaxis.

questions.question_text: Anterosuperior sternal part of heart is made up of?
questions.explanation: The right ventricle forms most of the anterior or sternocostal surface of the heart.

questions.question_text: Arch of aorta develops from which aortic arch artery?
questions.explanation: The left fourth aortic arch contributes to the arch of the aorta.

questions.question_text: Skin and fascia of great toe drain into?
questions.explanation: Most superficial lymphatics from the foot, including the great toe, follow the great saphenous vein to the superficial inguinal lymph nodes.

questions.question_text: Implantation occurs at?
questions.explanation: Implantation of the blastocyst into the endometrium usually begins around the sixth or seventh day after fertilization.

questions.question_text: Lower end of femur is ossified from how many ossification centres?
questions.explanation: The distal end of the femur has one secondary ossification centre, which appears around the ninth month of intrauterine life.

questions.question_text: Muscle of the third pharyngeal arch?
questions.explanation: Stylopharyngeus is the muscle derived from the third pharyngeal arch and is supplied by the glossopharyngeal nerve.

questions.question_text: Sinus venosus receives blood from all except?
questions.explanation: The embryonic sinus venosus receives blood from the vitelline, umbilical and common cardinal veins. The subcardinal veins are not direct tributaries.

questions.question_text: Cochleate uterus is?
questions.explanation: Cochleate uterus is described as an acutely anteflexed uterus, often with a small globular body and a pinhole cervical os.

questions.question_text: Which muscle originates from the tendon of another muscle?
questions.explanation: The lumbricals originate from the tendons of flexor digitorum profundus.

questions.question_text: True about anterior intercostal artery?

options.text: Present in the first to eleventh intercostal spaces
Each intercostal space has two anterior intercostal arteries

questions.explanation: Anterior intercostal arteries in the upper six spaces arise from the internal thoracic artery, while those in the seventh to ninth spaces arise from its musculophrenic branch.

questions.question_text: Medulla oblongata arises from?
questions.explanation: The medulla oblongata develops from the myelencephalon, which is part of the rhombencephalon.

questions.question_text: Interosseous membrane of forearm is pierced by?
questions.explanation: The anterior interosseous artery descends on the anterior surface of the interosseous membrane and pierces it near the upper border of pronator quadratus.

questions.question_text: Mastoid process is which type of epiphysis?
questions.explanation: The mastoid process is classified as a traction epiphysis because it develops in relation to muscle pull.

questions.question_text: Number of muscles in the middle ear?
questions.explanation: The middle ear contains two muscles: tensor tympani and stapedius.

questions.question_text: Ratio of connective tissue to smooth muscle in cervix is?
questions.explanation: The source gives the connective tissue to smooth muscle ratio in the cervix as approximately 8:1.

questions.question_text: Inferior epigastric artery forms the boundary of?
questions.explanation: The inferior epigastric vessels form the lateral boundary of Hesselbach's triangle.

questions.question_text: Superior wall of the middle ear is formed by?
questions.explanation: The roof of the middle ear cavity is formed by the tegmen tympani, a thin plate of temporal bone.

questions.question_text: Muscle causing flexion of hip?
questions.explanation: Psoas major is a powerful flexor of the hip joint and acts with iliacus as iliopsoas.

questions.question_text: Not true about facial vein is?
questions.explanation: The facial vein joins the anterior division of the retromandibular vein to form the common facial vein, which usually drains into the internal jugular vein.

questions.question_text: Structure passing through the superior orbital fissure?
questions.explanation: The superior orbital fissure transmits the oculomotor and trochlear nerves, ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve, abducens nerve and superior ophthalmic vein.

questions.question_text: Length of anal canal?
questions.explanation: The anal canal is approximately 3.8 to 4 cm long.

questions.question_text: Most common congenital anomaly of kidney?
questions.explanation: Horseshoe kidney is commonly described as the most frequent renal fusion anomaly. The source identifies it as the most common congenital renal anomaly.

questions.question_text: Sacral promontory is the landmark for?
questions.explanation: The presacral nerves terminate near the sacral promontory and continue as the right and left hypogastric nerves.

questions.question_text: Upper limb deformity in Erb's palsy?

options.text: Adduction and lateral rotation of arm
Adduction and medial rotation of arm
Abduction and lateral rotation of arm
Abduction and medial rotation of arm

questions.explanation: Erb's palsy causes the arm to hang by the side in adduction and medial rotation, with the forearm extended and pronated. This is called the policeman's tip posture.

questions.question_text: Cholecystocaval line separates?

options.text: Right and left functional lobes of liver
Right lobe of liver and gallbladder
Left lobe of liver and gallbladder

questions.explanation: The cholecystocaval line, an imaginary plane between the gallbladder fossa and inferior vena cava groove, separates the functional right and left lobes of the liver.

questions.question_text: Structure derived from the first pharyngeal arch?
questions.explanation: The anterior belly of digastric develops from the first pharyngeal arch and is supplied by the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve.

questions.question_text: Joint involved in movement of head from left to right?
questions.explanation: The atlanto-axial joint permits rotation of the head from side to side, as in the movement indicating 'no'.

questions.question_text: What is the nerve supply of the submandibular gland?
questions.explanation: Preganglionic parasympathetic fibres travel in the chorda tympani and join the lingual nerve before synapsing in the submandibular ganglion. Postganglionic fibres supply the gland.

questions.question_text: Parathyroid gland is implanted in which muscle?
questions.explanation: Parathyroid tissue may be autotransplanted into the brachioradialis muscle, commonly in the forearm, during selected parathyroid operations.

questions.question_text: Right coronary artery arises from?
questions.explanation: The right coronary artery arises from the right aortic sinus, also known as the anterior aortic sinus.

questions.question_text: Ducts of Bellini are present in?
questions.explanation: Ducts of Bellini are the papillary collecting ducts of the kidney, which open at the renal papilla into the minor calyces.

questions.question_text: Which of the following exocrine glandular ducts are not obstructed in cystic fibrosis?
questions.explanation: In cystic fibrosis, thick secretions obstruct ducts of mucus-secreting glands such as the pancreas and airways. Sweat gland ducts remain patent, although sweat has abnormally high chloride concentration.

questions.question_text: Boot shape of heart in TOF is due to:
questions.explanation: In Tetralogy of Fallot, right ventricular hypertrophy produces an upturned cardiac apex, creating the characteristic boot-shaped appearance on a chest radiograph.

questions.question_text: Which of the following structures is not derived from the external oblique muscle?
questions.explanation: The linea semilunaris is a curved tendinous line along the lateral border of rectus abdominis. The inguinal, lacunar and pectineal (Cooper) ligaments are derived from the external oblique aponeurosis.

questions.question_text: Contralateral loss of pain and temperature is due to injury to:
questions.explanation: The lateral spinothalamic tract carries pain and temperature sensations. Its fibers cross to the opposite side in the spinal cord, so injury causes contralateral loss below the lesion.

questions.question_text: Space of Disse is found in:
questions.explanation: The Space of Disse is the perisinusoidal space between hepatocytes and liver sinusoids. It contains blood plasma and receives hepatocyte microvilli.

questions.question_text: What are Gitter cells?
questions.explanation: Gitter cells are lipid-laden macrophages found in areas of CNS tissue damage. They phagocytose debris from degenerated myelin and damaged cells.

questions.question_text: Which syndrome is associated with posterior inferior cerebellar artery thrombosis?
questions.explanation: Wallenberg syndrome, also called lateral medullary syndrome, is classically associated with occlusion of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery or vertebral artery.

questions.question_text: Urethral crest is an elevation seen in the urethra due to:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the prostatic glands as the answer. The urethral crest is a longitudinal mucosal ridge on the posterior wall of the prostatic urethra, with prostatic sinuses on either side.

questions.question_text: Maxillary bone does not articulate with:
questions.explanation: The maxilla articulates with the frontal, ethmoid, nasal, zygomatic, lacrimal, inferior nasal concha, palatine, vomer and opposite maxilla. It does not normally articulate with the sphenoid.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about the location of the otic ganglion except:
questions.explanation: The otic ganglion lies medial to the mandibular nerve, just below the foramen ovale in the infratemporal fossa. It is functionally associated with the glossopharyngeal nerve and supplies secretomotor fibers to the parotid gland.

questions.question_text: In spermatogenesis, independent assortment of paternal and maternal chromosomes occurs during:
questions.explanation: Independent assortment occurs during meiosis I, when a primary spermatocyte divides to form two secondary spermatocytes.

questions.question_text: Sacrotuberous ligament is pierced by:
questions.explanation: The perforating cutaneous nerve, arising from the sacral plexus, pierces the sacrotuberous ligament and supplies skin over the lower medial part of the buttock.

questions.question_text: Lining epithelium of vagina is:
questions.explanation: The vaginal mucous membrane is lined by non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium.

questions.question_text: Tongue muscles are derived from:
questions.explanation: Most tongue muscles develop from occipital myotomes and are supplied by the hypoglossal nerve. Palatoglossus is an exception and is derived from the sixth pharyngeal arch.

questions.question_text: What is the insertion of levator scapulae?

options.text: Superior part of medial scapular border

questions.explanation: Levator scapulae originates from the posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C1–C4 and inserts on the superior part of the medial border of the scapula.

questions.question_text: Which muscle steadies the clavicle during movement of the shoulder?
questions.explanation: The subclavius muscle steadies and anchors the clavicle during movements of the shoulder.

questions.question_text: What is attached to the superior nuchal line?
questions.explanation: The trapezius attaches to the medial part of the superior nuchal line. Other muscles attached to this line include occipitalis, splenius capitis and sternocleidomastoid.

questions.question_text: Sensory supply of the palm is from which nerves?
questions.explanation: The median nerve supplies the lateral part of the palm, while the ulnar nerve supplies the medial part of the palm.

questions.question_text: What is the nerve supply of the cervical esophagus?
questions.explanation: The cervical esophagus receives parasympathetic innervation from the vagus nerves through both right and left recurrent laryngeal nerves.

questions.question_text: Which vein is found at the apex of the heart?
questions.explanation: The great cardiac vein begins at the apex of the heart and ascends along the anterior interventricular sulcus.

questions.question_text: Right hepatic vein drains which segment of the liver?
questions.explanation: The right hepatic vein drains the right functional liver, which includes segments V, VI, VII and VIII. Segment VII is therefore included in its drainage territory.

questions.question_text: Lymphatic drainage of the lateral wall of the nose is:
questions.explanation: The anterior half of the nasal cavity drains mainly to submandibular nodes. The posterior half drains to retropharyngeal and upper deep cervical nodes.

questions.question_text: The part of the neural tube from which the corpus callosum develops is:
questions.explanation: The corpus callosum develops from the lamina terminalis, the cranial part of the neural tube that later lies in the anterior wall of the third ventricle.

questions.question_text: Which gene is responsible for eye morphogenesis?
questions.explanation: PAX6 is a master control gene involved in eye development and morphogenesis. It encodes a transcription factor that regulates genes involved in eye formation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not attached to the medial border of the scapula?
questions.explanation: Serratus anterior, levator scapulae and rhomboid major attach to the medial border of the scapula. Teres major originates from the lateral border and inferior angle.

questions.question_text: The floor of Petit triangle is formed by:
questions.explanation: The floor of the inferior lumbar triangle (Petit triangle) is formed by the internal oblique muscle. Its other boundaries are the iliac crest, external oblique and latissimus dorsi.

questions.question_text: Which of the following arises from the infraglenoid tubercle?
questions.explanation: The long head of triceps brachii originates from the infraglenoid tubercle of the scapula. The long head of biceps originates from the supraglenoid tubercle.

questions.question_text: What is true about the adductors of the thigh?

options.text: Ischial head of adductor magnus is an adductor
Profunda femoris artery is the main blood supply
Ischial head of adductor magnus originates from the adductor tubercle
Adductor magnus is the largest muscle

questions.explanation: Adductor magnus is the largest muscle of the adductor compartment. Its hamstring part arises from the ischial tuberosity and is not considered an adductor part.

questions.question_text: All are supplied by the anterior interosseous nerve except:
questions.explanation: The anterior interosseous nerve supplies deep anterior forearm muscles, including flexor pollicis longus and the lateral half of flexor digitorum profundus. The listed exceptions are flexor carpi ulnaris, brachioradialis, abductor pollicis brevis and flexor digitorum superficialis.

questions.question_text: Teres minor is supplied by:
questions.explanation: The axillary nerve supplies the teres minor and deltoid muscles.

questions.question_text: What is the number of lobes in the breast?
questions.explanation: The breast is a modified sweat gland that typically consists of 15–20 lobes.

questions.question_text: What is the content of the anatomical snuffbox?
questions.explanation: The radial artery passes through the anatomical snuffbox. Its floor is formed by the scaphoid, trapezium and adjacent bones, and its tendinous boundaries are formed by thumb muscles.

questions.question_text: Abduction and adduction of the foot occur at which joint?
questions.explanation: Abduction and adduction of the foot occur mainly at the subtalar and midtarsal joints. The ankle joint primarily permits dorsiflexion and plantarflexion.

questions.question_text: What is the content of the femoral canal?
questions.explanation: The femoral canal contains lymphatics and the deep inguinal lymph node of Cloquet (Rosenmüller).

questions.question_text: The most common ligament damaged in knee injury is:
questions.explanation: The medial collateral ligament is commonly injured in knee trauma, particularly with a valgus force applied to the knee.

questions.question_text: What is the distance of the cricopharynx from the incisor teeth?
questions.explanation: The cricopharynx is at the pharyngoesophageal junction, approximately 15 cm from the upper incisor teeth. The cardiac end of the esophagus is approximately 40 cm away.

questions.question_text: All veins open into the sinus venarum except:
questions.explanation: The small cardiac vein generally drains into the coronary sinus. The source identifies it as not opening into the sinus venarum, the smooth posterior part of the right atrium.

questions.question_text: Which structure does not pass through the superior thoracic aperture?
questions.explanation: The right recurrent laryngeal nerve loops around the right subclavian artery in the root of the neck and ascends toward the larynx. It is not listed as a structure passing through the superior thoracic aperture.

questions.question_text: The common hepatic artery is a branch of:
questions.explanation: The common hepatic artery is one of the major branches of the coeliac trunk.

questions.question_text: Esophageal varices occur in which portion of the esophagus?
questions.explanation: Esophageal varices commonly occur at the lower end of the esophagus due to portosystemic (porto-caval) anastomoses.

questions.question_text: The anorectal angle is formed due to the action of:

options.text: Circular muscle layer of smooth muscle
Longitudinal muscle layer of smooth muscle

questions.explanation: The puborectalis muscle forms a sling around the anorectal junction. Its contraction makes the anorectal angle more acute and contributes to continence.

questions.question_text: The prostate analogue in females is:
questions.explanation: The paraurethral glands, also called Skene glands, are considered homologous to the prostate gland in males.

questions.question_text: The tail of the pancreas develops from:
questions.explanation: The dorsal pancreatic bud contributes to most of the pancreas, including the upper part of the head, body and tail. The ventral bud forms the uncinate process and lower part of the head.

questions.question_text: Haustrations are present in:
questions.explanation: Haustrations are sacculations characteristic of the large intestine. Other characteristic features include taeniae coli and appendices epiploicae.

questions.question_text: What is the anterior relation to the upper part of the rectum in males?
questions.explanation: In males, the upper two-thirds of the rectum is related anteriorly to the rectovesical pouch, which may contain coils of intestine and sigmoid colon.

questions.question_text: Sensory nerve supply of the gallbladder is through:
questions.explanation: The source identifies the vagus nerve. Gallbladder sensory pathways also involve sympathetic and phrenic nerves, which contribute to referred pain.

questions.question_text: Which ligament prevents the spleen from falling into the left iliac fossa?
questions.explanation: The phrenicocolic ligament and left colic flexure support the spleen and limit its downward enlargement toward the left iliac fossa.

questions.question_text: Labour pain in the uterus is carried by:
questions.explanation: Sympathetic fibers from the T10–L1 spinal segments carry pain sensations from the body of the uterus. Parasympathetic fibers from S2–S4 carry pain from the cervix.

questions.question_text: All are posterior relations of the right kidney except:
questions.explanation: The right kidney is related posteriorly to the 12th rib. The left kidney is related to both the 11th and 12th ribs.

questions.question_text: Which statement is not true about the blood supply of the kidney?

options.text: Renal vein drains into the inferior vena cava
Renal artery is a branch of the common iliac artery
Right renal artery passes behind the inferior vena cava
Branches of the renal artery are end arteries

questions.explanation: The renal arteries arise directly from the abdominal aorta, not the common iliac arteries. The right renal artery passes posterior to the inferior vena cava.

questions.question_text: The third part of the duodenum is not related to:
questions.explanation: The third part of the duodenum is related to the superior mesenteric vessels anteriorly, the right ureter and major vessels posteriorly, and the head of the pancreas superiorly. The quadrate lobe of the liver is not a relation.

questions.question_text: What is the correct sequence of uterine blood flow?

options.text: Uterine artery → Arcuate artery → Radial artery → Spiral artery
Uterine artery → Radial artery → Arcuate artery → Spiral artery
Uterine artery → Spiral artery → Radial artery → Arcuate artery
Uterine artery → Arcuate artery → Spiral artery → Radial artery

questions.explanation: The uterine artery gives arcuate arteries within the myometrium. These give rise to radial arteries, which terminate as spiral arterioles in the endometrium.

questions.question_text: The sternocleidomastoid muscle is examined by:

options.text: Turning the head towards the same side
Turning the head towards the opposite side

questions.explanation: Unilateral contraction of the sternocleidomastoid tilts the head toward the same side and rotates the face toward the opposite side.

questions.question_text: Stapedius pulls the stapes in which direction?
questions.explanation: Contraction of the stapedius muscle pulls the head of the stapes posteriorly and reduces the mobility of the ossicular chain.

questions.question_text: The major central nucleus of the sympathetic system is:
questions.explanation: The hypothalamus is the highest center for regulation of the autonomic nervous system, including both sympathetic and parasympathetic functions.

questions.question_text: The dangerous area of the scalp is:
questions.explanation: The loose areolar tissue beneath the epicranial aponeurosis is called the dangerous area of the scalp because emissary veins can allow infection to spread to intracranial venous sinuses.

questions.question_text: Which nerve is preserved when dissecting the superficial and deep lobes of the parotid gland?
questions.explanation: The facial nerve passes through the parotid gland and divides it into superficial and deep parts. It must be carefully identified and preserved during parotid surgery.

questions.question_text: Which intrinsic ocular muscle is supplied by parasympathetic innervation?
questions.explanation: The sphincter (constrictor) pupillae receives parasympathetic fibers from the Edinger–Westphal nucleus through the oculomotor nerve and ciliary ganglion. The dilator pupillae receives sympathetic innervation.

questions.question_text: The lips do not drain into which group of lymph nodes?
questions.explanation: Most of the upper lip and lateral lower lip drain into submandibular nodes, while the central lower lip drains into submental nodes. Preauricular parotid nodes are not the usual drainage group for the lips.

questions.question_text: Secretomotor fibers to the parotid gland pass through:
questions.explanation: Preganglionic parasympathetic fibers from the glossopharyngeal nerve reach the tympanic plexus, continue through the lesser petrosal nerve and synapse in the otic ganglion. Postganglionic fibers reach the parotid gland.

questions.question_text: Features of facial nerve palsy are all except:

options.text: Loss of taste sensation from posterior tongue

questions.explanation: Facial nerve palsy can cause weakness of facial expression, reduced lacrimation and salivation, and loss of taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue. Taste from the posterior one-third is carried by the glossopharyngeal nerve.

questions.question_text: The third ventricle is the cavity of:
questions.explanation: The third ventricle is the cavity of the diencephalon. The telencephalon contains the lateral ventricles, the midbrain contains the cerebral aqueduct, and the hindbrain contains the fourth ventricle.

questions.question_text: The oculomotor nucleus is located in:
questions.explanation: The oculomotor nucleus is located in the midbrain at the level of the superior colliculus.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a purely sensory nerve?
questions.explanation: The olfactory nerve (cranial nerve I) is a purely sensory nerve responsible for the sense of smell.

questions.question_text: The great cerebral vein of Galen drains into:
questions.explanation: The great cerebral vein of Galen is formed by the union of the two internal cerebral veins and drains into the straight sinus.

questions.question_text: The superficial middle cerebral vein drains into:
questions.explanation: The superficial middle cerebral vein runs along the lateral sulcus and commonly drains into the cavernous sinus. It communicates with other dural venous sinuses through anastomotic veins.

questions.question_text: What is the major arterial supply of the medial surface of the cerebral hemisphere?
questions.explanation: The anterior cerebral artery is the principal supply to the medial surface of the cerebral hemisphere. The middle cerebral artery mainly supplies the superolateral surface.

questions.question_text: Which nucleus is not seen in the floor of the fourth ventricle?
questions.explanation: The facial colliculus is visible in the floor of the fourth ventricle because facial nerve fibers loop around the abducens nucleus. The facial nucleus itself is located deeper in the pons and is not directly represented on the floor.

questions.question_text: Ventral tegmental decussation in the cerebral peduncle is due to:
questions.explanation: The ventral tegmental decussation is formed by crossing fibers of the rubrospinal tract. The dorsal tegmental decussation is associated with tectospinal and tectobulbar fibers.

questions.question_text: Oxyntic cells are present in:
questions.explanation: Oxyntic (parietal) cells are found mainly in the gastric glands of the fundus and body of the stomach. They secrete hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor.

questions.question_text: Which is the first bone to start ossifying?
questions.explanation: The source's explanation clarifies that the clavicle is the first bone to begin ossification and the mandible is among the next bones to ossify. Since the clavicle is not an option, the expected answer is mandible.

questions.question_text: Hilton's law is related to:
questions.explanation: Hilton's law states that the nerve supplying the muscles moving a joint also supplies the joint and the skin over the distal attachments of those muscles.

questions.question_text: Spermatogenesis begins at:
questions.explanation: Spermatogenesis begins at puberty and continues through adult life, with a gradual decline in old age.

questions.question_text: Which is not a stage of prophase I?
questions.explanation: The five recognized stages of prophase I are leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene and diakinesis. Arachytene is not a recognized stage.

questions.question_text: The fossa ovalis is a remnant of:
questions.explanation: The floor of the fossa ovalis represents the septum primum. The rim or limbus of the fossa ovalis is derived from the septum secundum.

questions.question_text: Fibrous stroma of the liver is derived from:
questions.explanation: The septum transversum mesenchyme contributes to the fibrous and supporting stroma of the liver, as well as Kupffer cells and hematopoietic tissue. Hepatocytes arise mainly from foregut endoderm.

questions.question_text: The heart tube is formed at:
questions.explanation: The primitive tubular heart forms during the third week of embryonic development and begins to function shortly afterward.

questions.question_text: The heart tube is formed in:
questions.explanation: Cardiac jelly is an extracellular matrix rich in hyaluronic acid. It is secreted by the myocardium and separates the endocardium from the myocardium.

questions.question_text: What is the remnant of the umbilical artery?
questions.explanation: The distal portions of the umbilical arteries become the medial umbilical ligaments. The proximal portions remain patent and contribute to the superior vesical arteries.

questions.question_text: Which statement is false about the limbus of the fossa ovalis?
questions.explanation: The limbus fossa ovalis, also called annulus ovalis, is a thickened rim in the right atrium derived from the septum secundum, not the septum primum.

questions.question_text: Sertoli cells are derived from:
questions.explanation: The germinal (coelomic) epithelium covering the genital ridge proliferates to form sex cords. Sertoli cells develop from these sex cords.

questions.question_text: Prolactin secreting gland develops from -
questions.explanation: The anterior lobe of the pituitary gland, which secretes prolactin, develops from Rathke's pouch.

questions.question_text: Posterior cardinal vein develops into -
questions.explanation: The right common iliac vein develops from the caudal part of the posterior cardinal vein. The left common iliac vein develops from an anastomosis between the lower ends of the posterior cardinal veins.

questions.question_text: Superior vena cava develops from -
questions.explanation: The superior vena cava develops from the right anterior cardinal vein proximal to the brachiocephalic anastomosis and the right common cardinal vein.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a derivative of Rathke's pouch -
questions.explanation: Rathke's pouch is an ectodermal upgrowth from the stomodeum and forms the anterior pituitary components, including pars distalis, pars intermedia and pars tuberalis.

questions.question_text: Which of glial cell is mesodermal in origin -
questions.explanation: Microglial cells are derived from mesenchymal cells of mesodermal origin.

questions.question_text: What structure passes through the quadrangular space?
questions.explanation: The axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral vessels pass through the quadrangular space.

questions.question_text: Lower limit of superior mediastinum is at which level -
questions.explanation: The superior and inferior mediastina are separated by the transverse thoracic plane passing through the sternal angle and the T4–T5 intervertebral disc. The source's printed answer appears to have a formatting or transcription error ('T1').

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not the muscles of superficial anterior compartment of forearm?
questions.explanation: Flexor pollicis longus is a deep anterior compartment muscle. The superficial group includes pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus, flexor digitorum superficialis and flexor carpi ulnaris.

questions.question_text: In case of aberrant obturator artery, it arises most commonly from?
questions.explanation: An aberrant or accessory obturator artery commonly arises from the inferior epigastric artery.

questions.question_text: Chief artery of lateral surface of cerebral hemisphere?
questions.explanation: The middle cerebral artery supplies most of the lateral surface of the cerebral hemisphere.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is remnant of distal umbilical artery?
questions.explanation: The distal parts of the umbilical arteries become the medial umbilical ligaments. Their proximal parts remain patent as superior vesical arteries.

questions.question_text: Female urethra develops from -
questions.explanation: The female urethra develops mainly from the pelvic part of the urogenital sinus.

questions.question_text: All of the following help in formation of IVC except -
