options.text: Terminal portion of right vitelline vein

questions.explanation: The IVC develops from several embryonic venous segments and anastomoses, including vitelline, subcardinal, supracardinal and posterior cardinal contributions. The source identifies the subcardinal sinus as the exception, although the wording is imprecise.

questions.question_text: Kidney parenchyma is derived from -
questions.explanation: The metanephric mesenchyme forms the nephrons and functional parenchyma of the definitive kidney. The ureteric bud forms the collecting system.

questions.question_text: Leptotene and pachytene are stages of which phases of meiosis -
questions.explanation: Leptotene and pachytene are stages of prophase I of meiosis. The five stages are leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene and diakinesis.

questions.question_text: Pelvic kidneys are due to all except?

options.text: Inability to ascend during fetal life
Being blocked by branches of the aorta

questions.explanation: An ectopic pelvic kidney results when a kidney fails to ascend during development, sometimes because of vascular obstruction. p53 mutation is not a cause.

questions.question_text: Crypta magna develops from which pouch?
questions.explanation: Crypta magna, or the intratonsillar cleft, represents persistence of the ventral part of the second pharyngeal pouch.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a traction epiphysis?
questions.explanation: The mastoid process is classically described as a traction epiphysis because it develops in association with muscle pull.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about the liver except?

options.text: It is covered by Glisson's capsule
Stellate cells are present in the space of Disse
Kupffer cells are the defense cells
The lobules in the liver are pentagonal

questions.explanation: The classical hepatic lobule is typically described as hexagonal, not pentagonal.

questions.question_text: Hering's canal is present in?
questions.explanation: The canals of Hering are small intrahepatic bile ductules that connect bile canaliculi with interlobular bile ducts.

questions.question_text: Herring's bodies are present in?
questions.explanation: Herring bodies are accumulations of neurosecretory material in axon terminals within the posterior pituitary, or neurohypophysis.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about thymus except?

options.text: The cortical portion is mainly composed of lymphocytes
It is derived from the fourth pharyngeal pouch
It undergoes atrophy from puberty onwards

questions.explanation: The thymus develops mainly from the third pharyngeal pouch, not the fourth. Its cortex contains numerous lymphocytes, its medulla contains Hassall's corpuscles, and it undergoes involution after puberty.

questions.question_text: Which of the following layers is absent in the esophagus?
questions.explanation: Most of the esophagus is covered by adventitia rather than serosa. A short abdominal segment has a serosal covering.

questions.question_text: Which is the most abundant cartilage?
questions.explanation: Hyaline cartilage is the most widely distributed and abundant type of cartilage in the body.

questions.question_text: What is the lining of the lacrimal gland alveoli?
questions.explanation: The secretory acini of the lacrimal gland are lined by pyramidal secretory cells.

questions.question_text: What type of muscles are medial two lumbricals?
questions.explanation: The medial two lumbricals of the hand are bipennate, arising from adjacent sides of the flexor digitorum profundus tendons.

questions.question_text: What is the level of the spine of scapula?
questions.explanation: The spine of the scapula is commonly level with the T3–T4 vertebral region, with its root approximately at T3.

questions.question_text: Which of the following muscles carries out shoulder abduction from 15 to 90 degrees?
questions.explanation: The deltoid is the principal muscle responsible for shoulder abduction from approximately 15 to 90 degrees. Supraspinatus initiates the first 15 degrees.

questions.question_text: Which muscle acting on the thumb has dual nerve supply?
questions.explanation: Flexor pollicis brevis has dual innervation: its superficial head is usually supplied by the recurrent branch of the median nerve and its deep head by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.

questions.question_text: What is Wartenberg's sign?

options.text: Inability to maintain intrinsic plus position
Inability to adduct small finger against the ring finger
Inability to grasp a book between the thumb and index finger
Inability to move the middle finger sideways

questions.explanation: Wartenberg's sign is the inability to adduct the little finger, often due to weakness or paralysis of the palmar interosseous muscle supplied by the ulnar nerve.

questions.question_text: Sensory region of the ulnar nerve is?
questions.explanation: The ulnar nerve supplies sensation to the little finger and the medial half of the ring finger, including their palmar and dorsal surfaces.

questions.question_text: Pulp of the index finger is supplied by
questions.explanation: The median nerve supplies the palmar surface and fingertip pulp of the lateral three and a half digits, including the index finger.

questions.question_text: Low radial nerve palsy [just after spiral groove] does not produce?
questions.explanation: In a radial nerve lesion distal to the spiral groove, the triceps is generally spared because its branches arise proximally. Elbow extension is therefore preserved.

questions.question_text: Infraspinous fossa of scapula contains which of the following muscles?
questions.explanation: The infraspinatus muscle arises from the infraspinous fossa of the scapula and inserts on the middle facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus.

questions.question_text: Coracoacromial ligament resists which movements?
questions.explanation: The coracoacromial arch forms a protective roof over the shoulder joint and resists superior displacement of the humeral head.

questions.question_text: Coracohumeral ligament inserts on?
questions.explanation: The coracohumeral ligament extends from the coracoid process to the greater and lesser tubercles of the humerus, spanning the intertubercular groove.

questions.question_text: What is the action of anconeus?
questions.explanation: The anconeus assists the triceps in elbow extension and helps stabilize the elbow joint.

questions.question_text: Which muscle helps in climbing a tree?
questions.explanation: Latissimus dorsi is commonly called the climber's muscle because it helps pull the trunk and body upward when climbing.

questions.question_text: Posterior interosseous artery is a branch of?
questions.explanation: The posterior interosseous artery usually arises from the common interosseous artery, a branch of the ulnar artery.

questions.question_text: Which muscle protects the brachial plexus in case of clavicle fractures?
questions.explanation: The subclavius muscle lies beneath the clavicle and can help protect the underlying subclavian vessels and brachial plexus from injury.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about deep palmar arch?

options.text: Mainly formed by the radial artery
Ulnar artery has no contribution to it
It does not anastomose with the superficial palmar arch

questions.explanation: The deep palmar arch is formed mainly by the radial artery and is completed by the deep branch of the ulnar artery.

questions.question_text: Which part of scapula can be palpated in the infraclavicular fossa?
questions.explanation: The coracoid process is palpable just inferior to the lateral part of the clavicle in the infraclavicular region.

questions.question_text: Flexor carpi radialis inserts into?
questions.explanation: Flexor carpi radialis inserts mainly at the bases of the second and third metacarpal bones.

questions.question_text: What is true about lateral tibial condyle?

options.text: Iliotibial tract is attached to the lateral condyle of tibia
Medial collateral ligament is attached to it

questions.explanation: The iliotibial tract inserts at Gerdy's tubercle on the anterolateral aspect of the proximal tibia, near the lateral condyle.

questions.question_text: Weakness of extensor hallucis longus is due to which nerve root mainly?
questions.explanation: The extensor hallucis longus is predominantly supplied by the L5 nerve root through the deep fibular nerve.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is common between the medial and lateral plantar arch?
questions.explanation: The plantar aponeurosis acts as a tie beam supporting both the medial and lateral longitudinal arches of the foot.

questions.question_text: Which tendon is lodged in the groove on posterior surface of lateral malleolus?
questions.explanation: The tendons of fibularis longus and brevis pass behind the lateral malleolus in the retromalleolar groove.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about tibialis anterior except?

options.text: It is supplied by the superficial peroneal nerve
It is closely related to the anterior tibial vessels
It inserts on the medial cuneiform

questions.explanation: Tibialis anterior is supplied by the deep fibular (peroneal) nerve, not the superficial fibular nerve. It dorsiflexes and inverts the foot and inserts on the medial cuneiform and base of the first metatarsal.

questions.question_text: Attachment on posterior surface of sacrum?
questions.explanation: The multifidus has attachments to the posterior sacrum and extends to the transverse and articular processes of superior vertebrae.

questions.question_text: Structures passing through sacral hiatus are?
questions.explanation: The sacral hiatus is the inferior opening of the sacral canal, usually at the level of S5. The sacral and coccygeal nerve roots and filum terminale pass through the canal and exit inferiorly.

questions.question_text: Longest cutaneous nerve in body?
questions.explanation: The saphenous nerve, a sensory branch of the femoral nerve, is the longest cutaneous nerve. It supplies the medial leg and medial border of the foot.

questions.question_text: Oblique popliteal ligament is derived from?
questions.explanation: The oblique popliteal ligament is an expansion of the tendon of semimembranosus.

questions.question_text: Lateral border of the foot receives its sensory supply from?
questions.explanation: The sural nerve supplies the skin along the lateral border of the foot and the lateral side of the little toe.

questions.question_text: All of the following is included in chest wall except?
questions.explanation: The thoracic wall is formed by the sternum, ribs, costal cartilages, thoracic vertebrae and associated muscles. Lumbar vertebrae are not part of the chest wall.

questions.question_text: Respiratory bronchioles are formed from?
questions.explanation: Terminal bronchioles give rise to respiratory bronchioles, which continue into alveolar ducts and alveolar sacs.

questions.question_text: Segment of bronchi distal to primary bifurcation?
questions.explanation: Each primary bronchus divides into secondary, or lobar, bronchi. The source's marked answer 'primary bronchi' does not match the wording of the question.

questions.question_text: The cricopharyngeal sphincter is how far from the central incisor?
questions.explanation: The upper esophageal sphincter at the cricopharyngeus is approximately 15 cm from the upper incisor teeth.

questions.question_text: Which of the following structures is related to the esophagus 22.5 cm from the incisor teeth?
questions.explanation: The arch of the aorta crosses and produces an impression on the esophagus at approximately 22.5 cm from the incisors.

questions.question_text: Thoracic duct opens into systemic circulation at?

options.text: Junction of SVC and left brachiocephalic vein
Junction of left internal jugular and left subclavian vein

questions.explanation: The thoracic duct usually terminates at the left venous angle, where the left internal jugular and left subclavian veins unite.

questions.question_text: Sympathetic supply of the heart is from?
questions.explanation: Preganglionic sympathetic fibres supplying the heart arise mainly from spinal cord segments T1–T5 and reach the cardiac plexus through cervical and upper thoracic sympathetic pathways.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are cusps of the aortic valves?
questions.explanation: The aortic valve has three semilunar cusps: right coronary, left coronary and non-coronary (posterior) cusps.

questions.question_text: Which is the widow's artery in myocardial infarction?
questions.explanation: The left anterior descending artery supplies a large portion of the anterior left ventricle and interventricular septum. Its acute occlusion can cause a large, life-threatening myocardial infarction.

questions.question_text: Which of the following passes posterior to the hilum of the lung?
questions.explanation: The vagus nerve passes posterior to the root of the lung, whereas the phrenic nerve passes anterior to it.

questions.question_text: What is the level of the pulmonary valve?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary valve is located behind the medial end of the third left costal cartilage, near the sternum.

questions.question_text: Lower limit of the inferior border of the lung in the midaxillary line is?
questions.explanation: The inferior border of the lung crosses the eighth rib in the midaxillary line. The pleural reflection is approximately two ribs lower, at the tenth rib.

questions.question_text: Great cardiac vein lies in?
questions.explanation: The great cardiac vein accompanies the anterior interventricular artery in the anterior interventricular sulcus.

questions.question_text: Apex of the lung lies at what level?

options.text: At the level of the clavicle

questions.explanation: The apex of the lung projects into the root of the neck, approximately 2–3 cm above the medial third of the clavicle.

questions.question_text: Diaphragm is supplied by?
questions.explanation: The diaphragm receives motor supply from the phrenic nerves, which arise from C3, C4 and C5. Peripheral sensory supply is carried by lower intercostal nerves.

questions.question_text: Midpoint between suprasternal notch and pubic symphysis passes through which plane?
questions.explanation: The transpyloric plane is classically described as midway between the suprasternal notch and pubic symphysis. It passes approximately through the L1 vertebral level.

questions.question_text: Muscle lying between anterior and middle layer of thoracolumbar fascia is?
questions.explanation: Quadratus lumborum lies between the anterior and middle layers of the thoracolumbar fascia. The erector spinae group lies between the middle and posterior layers.

questions.question_text: Anterior rectus sheath just above pubic symphysis is formed by?

options.text: The aponeurosis of three muscles including external oblique, internal oblique, and transversus abdominis

questions.explanation: Below the arcuate line, the aponeuroses of the external oblique, internal oblique and transversus abdominis all pass anterior to the rectus abdominis, forming the anterior rectus sheath.

questions.question_text: Right suprarenal vein drains into?
questions.explanation: The right suprarenal vein drains directly into the inferior vena cava. The left suprarenal vein usually drains into the left renal vein.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not derived from the external oblique aponeurosis?
questions.explanation: The linea semilunaris is the curved tendinous line marking the lateral border of rectus abdominis. The inguinal, lacunar and pectineal ligaments are related to the external oblique aponeurosis.

questions.question_text: Stomach wall is mainly drained by all lymph nodes except?
questions.explanation: Lymph from the stomach drains through gastric, pyloric, gastroepiploic and pancreaticosplenic nodal groups, ultimately reaching the coeliac nodes. Inguinal nodes are not part of this drainage pathway.

questions.question_text: All lymph of stomach drains into?
questions.explanation: Lymphatic drainage from the stomach ultimately reaches the coeliac lymph nodes before passing into the intestinal lymph trunks and thoracic duct.

questions.question_text: Gall bladder is related to which segment of the liver?
questions.explanation: The gallbladder lies in a fossa on the visceral surface of the liver, associated with the region of segment IV and the quadrate lobe.

questions.question_text: Which segment of liver drains on both sides?
questions.explanation: Segment I, the caudate lobe, has independent vascular and biliary drainage, receiving branches from both sides and draining into both right and left hepatic ducts.

questions.question_text: Caudate lobe of the liver - True is?

options.text: It receives blood supply from both right and left hepatic arteries
It is segment II of the liver
It is situated on the anterior surface of liver
It lies between the aorta and ligamentum venosum

questions.explanation: The caudate lobe is segment I, situated on the posterior surface of the liver between the inferior vena cava and ligamentum venosum. It may receive branches from both right and left hepatic arteries.

questions.question_text: Superior border of epiploic foramen formed by -
questions.explanation: The superior boundary of the epiploic foramen (foramen of Winslow) is formed by the caudate lobe of the liver.

questions.question_text: Internal anal sphincter is formed by?
questions.explanation: The internal anal sphincter is a thickening of the circular smooth muscle layer of the rectum at the anal canal. It is involuntary.

questions.question_text: Which muscle causes opening of the upper end of esophagus?
questions.explanation: The cricopharyngeus forms the main component of the upper esophageal sphincter. It relaxes during swallowing to allow food to enter the esophagus.

questions.question_text: Posterior perforation of stomach, collection of contents occurs in which pouch?

options.text: Left subhepatic and hepatorenal spaces (pouch of Morrison)

questions.explanation: A posterior gastric perforation may initially release contents into the lesser sac, also called the omental bursa. The contents may subsequently pass through the epiploic foramen into the hepatorenal recess.

questions.question_text: Cremasteric muscle is formed from?
questions.explanation: The cremaster muscle and fascia are derived mainly from the internal oblique muscle and its fascia.

questions.question_text: Kidney is covered by what fascia?
questions.explanation: The renal fascia, commonly called Gerota's fascia, surrounds the kidney and perirenal fat.

questions.question_text: Narrowest part of ureter is?
questions.explanation: The vesicoureteric junction, where the ureter enters the bladder wall, is the narrowest part of the ureter.

questions.question_text: What is the total length of the colon?
questions.explanation: The large intestine is approximately 1.5 metres long. The colon forms its major portion.

questions.question_text: Submandibular lymph nodes drain the following areas of the face except?
questions.explanation: The central part of the lower lip and chin drain mainly into the submental lymph nodes, not the submandibular nodes.

questions.question_text: Larynx below the vocal cords drains into?

options.text: Lymphatics along the superior laryngeal vein

questions.explanation: The infraglottic part of the larynx drains mainly into pretracheal and prelaryngeal lymph nodes.

questions.question_text: Nerve supply to the angle of the mandible is by?

options.text: Posterior primary rami of C2, C3

questions.explanation: The greater auricular nerve, arising from the cervical plexus (C2–C3), supplies the skin over the angle of the mandible.

questions.question_text: Nerve supply to the tip of the nose is from?

options.text: The ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve
The maxillary division of the trigeminal nerve

questions.explanation: The tip of the nose is supplied by the external nasal branch of the anterior ethmoidal nerve, a branch of the ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve.

questions.question_text: Dangerous space in the neck is found between?
questions.explanation: The danger space lies between the alar fascia anteriorly and the prevertebral fascia posteriorly. It extends from the skull base to the diaphragm.

questions.question_text: Which muscle is attached to the disc of the temporomandibular joint?
questions.explanation: The superior head of the lateral pterygoid attaches to the articular disc and capsule of the temporomandibular joint.

questions.question_text: Maxillary tubercle gives attachment to?
questions.explanation: The superficial head of the medial pterygoid arises partly from the maxillary tuberosity.

questions.question_text: Vidian nerve is also known as?
questions.explanation: The Vidian nerve is the nerve of the pterygoid canal, formed by the union of the greater petrosal and deep petrosal nerves.

questions.question_text: Right recurrent laryngeal nerve loops around?
questions.explanation: The right recurrent laryngeal nerve loops under the right subclavian artery before ascending in the tracheoesophageal groove.

questions.question_text: Left recurrent laryngeal nerve passes between?
questions.explanation: The left recurrent laryngeal nerve ascends in the groove between the trachea and esophagus.

questions.question_text: Structures pierced by the parotid duct are all except?

options.text: Investing layer of deep cervical fascia

questions.explanation: The parotid duct passes through the buccal fat pad, buccopharyngeal fascia and buccinator muscle. It does not pierce the investing layer of deep cervical fascia.

questions.question_text: Which layer of the scalp is vascular?
questions.explanation: The dense connective tissue layer, or superficial fascia, contains numerous blood vessels that are held open by fibrous septa.

questions.question_text: All of the following pass through the sinus of Morgagni except?
questions.explanation: The sinus of Morgagni is a gap above the superior constrictor. The auditory tube, levator veli palatini and associated vessels pass through it. Stylopharyngeus passes between the superior and middle constrictors.

questions.question_text: Chorda tympani is a branch of?
questions.explanation: The chorda tympani is a branch of the facial nerve (cranial nerve VII). It carries taste fibres from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue and preganglionic parasympathetic fibres.

questions.question_text: Chorda tympani does not carry which fibers?

options.text: Preganglionic parasympathetic fibers for sublingual glands
Preganglionic parasympathetic fibers for submandibular gland
Preganglionic parasympathetic fibers for parotid gland
Taste fibers from anterior two-thirds of tongue

questions.explanation: The chorda tympani carries taste fibres and preganglionic parasympathetic fibres for the submandibular and sublingual glands. Parotid secretomotor fibres travel through the glossopharyngeal and lesser petrosal nerves.

questions.question_text: Which of the following passes through the hypoglossal canal?
questions.explanation: The hypoglossal nerve (cranial nerve XII) passes through the hypoglossal canal to reach the tongue.

questions.question_text: Which muscle is antagonist to orbicularis oculi that is not supplied by facial nerve?
questions.explanation: Orbicularis oculi closes the eyelids and is supplied by the facial nerve. Levator palpebrae superioris opens the upper eyelid and is supplied by the oculomotor nerve.

questions.question_text: All of the following are main branches of the trigeminal nerve except?
questions.explanation: The trigeminal nerve has three divisions: ophthalmic (V1), maxillary (V2) and mandibular (V3). The optic nerve is cranial nerve II.

questions.question_text: Extension of the retropharyngeal space is between?
questions.explanation: The retropharyngeal space lies between the buccopharyngeal fascia anteriorly and alar fascia posteriorly. The danger space lies between the alar and prevertebral fasciae.

questions.question_text: Delphian nodes are?
questions.explanation: The Delphian node is the prelaryngeal lymph node located anterior to the larynx, near the cricothyroid membrane.

questions.question_text: Straight sinus is formed by?
questions.explanation: The straight sinus is formed by the union of the inferior sagittal sinus and great cerebral vein.

questions.question_text: Which artery supplies the paracentral lobule?
questions.explanation: The callosomarginal artery, a branch of the anterior cerebral artery, supplies much of the paracentral lobule.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a permanent mucosal fold?
questions.explanation: Gastric rugae are temporary folds that flatten when the stomach distends. Plicae circulares and the spiral folds of the cystic duct are relatively permanent.

questions.question_text: Most lateral nucleus of cerebellum is?
questions.explanation: The dentate nucleus is the most lateral of the four deep cerebellar nuclei.

questions.question_text: Superior marginal gyrus is a part of?
questions.explanation: The supramarginal gyrus is part of the inferior parietal lobule of the parietal lobe.

questions.question_text: Spinal segmental artery is a branch of?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the ascending spinal artery. Segmental medullary arteries, however, arise from regional segmental vessels and reinforce the longitudinal spinal arteries; the terminology in the question is unclear.

questions.question_text: Pars dorsalis is a part of?
questions.explanation: Pars dorsalis refers to the dorsal part of the pons, associated with the pontine tegmentum.

questions.question_text: Movement occurring at atlanto-axial joint?
questions.explanation: The atlanto-axial joints permit rotation of the head, as when turning the head from side to side.

questions.question_text: Arbor vitae are seen in?
questions.explanation: Arbor vitae is the branching pattern of white matter within the cerebellum.

questions.question_text: Long spinous process is seen in?
questions.explanation: Typical thoracic vertebrae have long, inferiorly directed spinous processes.

questions.question_text: Total volume of CSF is?
questions.explanation: The total cerebrospinal fluid volume in an adult is approximately 125–150 ml.

questions.question_text: Lateral lemniscus terminates into?
questions.explanation: The lateral lemniscus carries auditory information to the inferior colliculus of the midbrain.

questions.question_text: Cerebellovestibular fibres pass through?
questions.explanation: Vestibulocerebellar fibres pass through the inferior cerebellar peduncle.

questions.question_text: Internal capsule: all of the following are parts except?
questions.explanation: The internal capsule is divided into anterior limb, genu, posterior limb, retrolentiform part and sublentiform part. Prelentiform is not a standard division.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is derived from the neural tube except?
questions.explanation: Dorsal root ganglia develop from neural crest cells, whereas the brain, retina and pineal gland are derived from neuroectoderm of the neural tube.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a complete sulcus in the brain?
questions.explanation: The calcarine sulcus is a complete sulcus because its floor is elevated into the posterior horn of the lateral ventricle.

questions.question_text: Substantia ferruginea is found in?
questions.explanation: Substantia ferruginea, also called locus coeruleus or locus caeruleus region, is visible in the floor of the fourth ventricle near its lateral part.

questions.question_text: Infundibular diverticulum is an extension of?
questions.explanation: The infundibular recess is a downward extension of the third ventricle into the infundibulum of the hypothalamus.

questions.question_text: Osseocartilaginous junction is present at?
questions.explanation: The rhinion is the anatomical landmark at the junction of the nasal bones and upper lateral nasal cartilages.

questions.question_text: At what level does the trachea bifurcate?
questions.explanation: The trachea usually bifurcates at the carina around the sternal angle, approximately at the T4–T5 intervertebral disc level.

questions.question_text: Cricoid cartilage lies at which vertebral level?
questions.explanation: The cricoid cartilage lies approximately at the level of the C6 vertebra.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about vertebral development?

options.text: The notochord forms the annulus fibrosus
The sclerotome forms the nucleus pulposus
The sclerotome surrounds the notochord only
The sclerotome surrounds the notochord and the neural tube

questions.explanation: Sclerotomes surround both the notochord and neural tube. The notochord contributes to the nucleus pulposus, while the sclerotomes form the vertebrae and annulus fibrosus.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a congenital anomaly?
questions.explanation: Mastitis is inflammation of breast tissue, not a congenital developmental anomaly. Amastia, polymastia and polythelia are congenital anomalies.

questions.question_text: Rectum develops from?
questions.explanation: The rectum develops from the hindgut. Its terminal portion is associated with the posterior part of the cloaca, separated from the urogenital sinus by the urorectal septum.

questions.question_text: All are derived from ectoderm except?
questions.explanation: The adrenal cortex develops from mesoderm. The adrenal medulla develops from neural crest cells, while the pituitary, retina and spinal cord have ectodermal origins.

questions.question_text: Development of labia majora is from?
questions.explanation: The genital swellings develop into the labia majora in females and the scrotum in males.

questions.question_text: Blastocyst makes contact with endometrium on?
questions.explanation: The blastocyst typically begins implantation by attaching to the endometrium around day 6–7 after fertilization.

questions.question_text: Haploid number of chromosomes is seen in?
questions.explanation: Secondary spermatocytes are haploid cells containing 23 chromosomes after completion of meiosis I.

questions.question_text: Which sperm chromosome is faster?
questions.explanation: The source marks Y-bearing sperm as faster, based on the traditional teaching that they are lighter. However, reliable evidence does not establish a consistent speed difference between X-bearing and Y-bearing sperm.

questions.question_text: All are derived from ectoderm except?
questions.explanation: The Eustachian tube develops from the first pharyngeal pouch, which is endodermal in origin. The lens, brain and retina are ectodermal derivatives.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is derived from endoderm?
questions.explanation: The epithelial lining and glandular components of the gallbladder develop from endoderm of the foregut.

questions.question_text: Development of peritoneal cavity is from?
questions.explanation: The peritoneal cavity develops from the intraembryonic coelom formed within the lateral plate mesoderm.

questions.question_text: Cytotrophoblasts invade?
questions.explanation: During placental development, trophoblastic cells invade the maternal endometrium, particularly the decidua basalis. The source specifically identifies cytotrophoblasts.

questions.question_text: Coronary sinus develops from?
questions.explanation: The coronary sinus develops mainly from the left horn of the sinus venosus.

questions.question_text: Which is derived from Wolffian duct?
questions.explanation: The appendix of the epididymis is a remnant of the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct. The appendix of the testis is a remnant of the paramesonephric duct.

questions.question_text: Artery of second pharyngeal arch is?
questions.explanation: The second aortic arch gives rise to the stapedial and hyoid arteries, which largely regress.

questions.question_text: Fossa ovalis is a remnant of?
questions.explanation: The floor of the fossa ovalis is formed by the remnant of the septum primum. Its raised margin is related to the septum secundum.

questions.question_text: Y chromosome is?
questions.explanation: The human Y chromosome is classified as acrocentric, with its centromere located close to one end.

questions.question_text: The outer layer of the blastocyst forms?
questions.explanation: The outer cell layer of the blastocyst is the trophoblast, which contributes to the fetal component of the placenta.

questions.question_text: Inferior parathyroid develops from which pharyngeal pouch?
questions.explanation: The inferior parathyroid glands develop from the dorsal wing of the third pharyngeal pouch, along with the thymus from its ventral wing.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is mesodermal in origin?
questions.explanation: Microglial cells originate from mesoderm-derived myeloid precursor cells. Most other central nervous system glial cells arise from neuroectoderm.

questions.question_text: Fossa ovalis closes because of fusion of?
questions.explanation: After birth, increased left atrial pressure presses the septum primum against the septum secundum, leading to functional and often anatomical closure of the foramen ovale.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a traction epiphysis?
questions.explanation: The greater and lesser trochanters of the femur are traction apophyses associated with muscle attachment and pull.

questions.question_text: Corpora arenacea is seen in?
questions.explanation: Corpora arenacea, also called brain sand, are calcified deposits commonly found in the pineal gland.

questions.question_text: Nutrient artery runs?
questions.explanation: The nutrient artery enters the shaft of a long bone and divides into ascending and descending branches that course toward the metaphyses.

questions.question_text: Multi-unit smooth muscle is present at all except?
questions.explanation: The gut predominantly contains single-unit (visceral) smooth muscle, in which cells are electrically coupled by gap junctions.

questions.question_text: Renal papilla opens into?
questions.explanation: The apex of each renal pyramid forms a renal papilla, which projects into a minor calyx.

questions.question_text: Following a deep cut overlying the hypothenar eminence, it is observed that the patient cannot hold a sheet of paper between the 2nd and 3rd digits. Which of the following nerves is most likely damaged?

options.text: Deep branch of the radial nerve

questions.explanation: The deep branch of the ulnar nerve supplies the palmar interossei, which adduct the fingers. Damage can impair the ability to hold paper between adjacent fingers.

questions.question_text: During heel touch phase of walking, pressure in calf compartment is?
questions.explanation: The source states that calf compartment pressure does not change during heel strike, when the posterior calf muscles are not actively contracting strongly.

questions.question_text: The nutrient artery to the femur is?
questions.explanation: The nutrient artery of the femur commonly arises from a perforating branch of the profunda femoris artery.

questions.question_text: Site of injection in gluteus?
questions.explanation: The traditional dorsogluteal intramuscular injection site is the upper outer quadrant of the buttock to reduce the risk of injury to the sciatic nerve and major gluteal vessels. Ventrogluteal sites are generally preferred in current practice.

questions.question_text: Waldeyer's fascia lies?
questions.explanation: Waldeyer's fascia, also known as the presacral fascia, lies posterior to the rectum and separates it from the sacrum and presacral structures.

questions.question_text: The transverse sinus is present posterior to which structures?
questions.explanation: The transverse pericardial sinus lies posterior to the ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk, and anterior to the superior vena cava and left atrium. The question's wording is imprecise because it asks what lies posterior to the sinus.

questions.question_text: Surface marking of the oblique fissure of the lung includes all except?
questions.explanation: The oblique fissure is marked from the level of T3 posteriorly, crossing the fifth rib in the midaxillary line and reaching the sixth costal cartilage anteriorly. The seventh rib is not one of the stated landmarks.

questions.question_text: Anterior relations of the right kidney are all except?
questions.explanation: The anterior relations of the right kidney include the liver, second part of the duodenum, hepatic flexure and suprarenal gland. The fourth part of the duodenum is not a relation.

questions.question_text: Pancreas divisum indicates which of the following?

options.text: Failure of fusion of dorsal and ventral pancreatic buds
Formation of more than two pancreatic buds
Formation of only one pancreatic bud

questions.explanation: Pancreas divisum results from failure of fusion of the dorsal and ventral pancreatic buds and their duct systems.

questions.question_text: Right ovarian artery is a branch of?
questions.explanation: The ovarian arteries arise directly from the abdominal aorta, usually below the renal arteries.

questions.question_text: Structure immediately posterior to pancreatic head?
questions.explanation: The terminal part of the right renal vein is related posteriorly to the head of the pancreas.

questions.question_text: Which of these best describes the renal angle?

options.text: The angle between the latissimus dorsi and the 12th rib
The angle between the erector spinae and the iliac crest
The angle between the 12th rib and the erector spinae
The angle between the 12th rib and the rectus abdominis

questions.explanation: The renal angle is formed between the lower border of the 12th rib and the lateral border of the erector spinae muscle.

questions.question_text: In patients with penile injury, Colles' fascia prevents extravasation of urine in?
questions.explanation: Colles' fascia attaches to the perineal boundaries and helps prevent urine from spreading into the ischioanal fossae.

questions.question_text: Neurovascular plane in anterior abdominal wall is?

options.text: Between external oblique and internal oblique
Between internal oblique and transversus abdominis

questions.explanation: The neurovascular plane of the anterolateral abdominal wall lies between the internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles.

questions.question_text: In bladder injury, pain is referred to all except?
questions.explanation: Bladder pain may be referred to the lower abdominal wall, upper thighs, external genitalia and perineum. Flank pain is not a typical referred site.

questions.question_text: Structure not seen at L3 level?
questions.explanation: The coeliac trunk arises around the T12 level and is not normally seen at L3.

questions.question_text: Spleen extends from?
questions.explanation: The spleen lies deep to the left 9th, 10th and 11th ribs, with its long axis corresponding approximately to the 10th rib.

questions.question_text: All are branches of the inferior mesenteric artery except?
questions.explanation: The inferior mesenteric artery gives rise to the left colic, sigmoid and superior rectal arteries. The middle rectal artery usually arises from the internal iliac artery.

questions.question_text: Rouviere nodes are situated in?
questions.explanation: Rouviere's node is the superior-most node of the lateral group of retropharyngeal lymph nodes, near the base of the skull.

questions.question_text: Risorius is a muscle of?
questions.explanation: Risorius is a muscle of facial expression that pulls the angle of the mouth laterally.

questions.question_text: The thyrocervical trunk is a branch of which part of the subclavian artery?
questions.explanation: The thyrocervical trunk usually arises from the first part of the subclavian artery.

questions.question_text: Nucleus fasciculatus is seen in?
questions.explanation: The source identifies this as a nucleus in the medulla associated with the dorsal column pathway. The term nucleus fasciculatus is not standard; it may refer to the nucleus cuneatus.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an operculated sulcus?
questions.explanation: The lunate sulcus is described as an operculated sulcus, separating striate and parastriate cortical areas.

questions.question_text: Chamberlain's line is?
questions.explanation: Chamberlain's line is drawn from the posterior margin of the hard palate to the opisthion, the posterior margin of the foramen magnum.

questions.question_text: Structures not passing through aortic opening?
questions.explanation: The aorta, thoracic duct and often the azygos vein pass through the aortic hiatus at T12. The vagal trunks pass through the oesophageal hiatus.

questions.question_text: Nerves of branchial arch derived from?
questions.explanation: Neural crest cells contribute extensively to the cranial ganglia and peripheral neural components associated with the pharyngeal arches. The question is broad because the nerves themselves also contain neuroectoderm-derived components.

questions.question_text: Acute tonsillitis affects which nerve?
questions.explanation: The glossopharyngeal nerve supplies the palatine tonsil through tonsillar branches and may be affected during tonsillar procedures.

questions.question_text: Hard palate contains?

options.text: Keratinised epithelium, submucosa, minor salivary glands
Keratinised epithelium, absent submucosal layer, minor salivary glands
Non-keratinised epithelium, submucosal layer, minor salivary glands
Non-keratinised epithelium, absent submucosa, minor salivary glands

questions.explanation: The hard palate is lined by keratinised stratified squamous epithelium. Submucosa is present particularly in the posterolateral regions and contains minor salivary glands.

questions.question_text: Broca's area is situated in?
questions.explanation: Broca's area is located in the posterior part of the inferior frontal gyrus of the dominant cerebral hemisphere, usually the left.

questions.question_text: Thrombosis of posterior inferior cerebellar artery causes?
questions.explanation: Occlusion of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery commonly causes lateral medullary syndrome, also known as Wallenberg syndrome.

questions.question_text: What is the tensor of vocal cords?
questions.explanation: The cricothyroid muscle tenses and lengthens the vocal folds by tilting the thyroid cartilage forward.

questions.question_text: About Sibson's fascia, which is incorrect?

options.text: Attached to the inner border of 2nd rib

questions.explanation: Sibson's fascia, or the suprapleural membrane, covers the lung apex and attaches to the inner border of the first rib and the transverse process of C7.

questions.question_text: Ureteric bud develops from?
questions.explanation: The ureteric bud arises as an outgrowth of the mesonephric duct. It forms the ureter, renal pelvis, major and minor calyces, and collecting ducts.

questions.question_text: About Weber's syndrome, which is incorrect?
questions.explanation: Weber syndrome results from a lesion of the ventral midbrain involving the oculomotor fascicles and cerebral peduncle. The term 'anterior cerebral peduncle' is not the correct anatomical description.

questions.question_text: All are special visceral efferent nerves except?
questions.explanation: The nucleus ambiguus is a motor nucleus that gives rise to special visceral efferent fibres; it is not a nerve. The trigeminal, glossopharyngeal and vagus nerves carry special visceral efferent fibres.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true about iliolumbar ligament?

options.text: Upper fibres attached to iliac crest
Lower fibres attached to base of sacrum
Helps in maintaining lumbosacral joint stability
Upper attachment to transverse process of T12

questions.explanation: The iliolumbar ligament extends from the transverse process of L5 to the iliac crest, with some fibres attaching to the sacrum. It does not attach to T12.

questions.question_text: Which of the following structures develops from dorsal mesentery?
questions.explanation: The dorsal mesogastrium, a part of the dorsal mesentery, develops into the greater omentum.

questions.question_text: Chordoma arises from?
questions.explanation: Chordoma is a tumour arising from remnants of the embryonic notochord, commonly occurring at the skull base or sacrum.

questions.question_text: Seminal colliculus is present in?
questions.explanation: The seminal colliculus, or verumontanum, is an elevation on the urethral crest within the prostatic urethra.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a derivative of foregut?
questions.explanation: The cecum develops from the midgut. The foregut gives rise to the stomach, proximal duodenum, liver and pancreas, among other structures.

questions.question_text: Upward movement of the thyroid gland is prevented due to?
questions.explanation: The pretracheal fascia attaches the thyroid gland to the laryngeal framework and trachea. Berry's ligament is a thickening of this fascial attachment and helps the gland move during swallowing.

questions.question_text: The reason for the long left recurrent laryngeal nerve is due to the persistence of which arch artery?
questions.explanation: The left recurrent laryngeal nerve loops under the arch of the aorta, which develops from the left fourth aortic arch.

questions.question_text: Ligation of the hepatic artery will impair blood supply in?

options.text: Right gastric and right gastroepiploic artery
Right gastric and left gastric artery
Right gastroepiploic and short gastric vessels
Right gastric and short gastric vessels

questions.explanation: The right gastric artery usually arises from the hepatic artery, while the right gastroepiploic artery arises from the gastroduodenal artery, a branch of the common hepatic artery. The left gastric and short gastric arteries arise from the coeliac system independently.

questions.question_text: Wolffian duct remnant in female is?
questions.explanation: Gartner's duct cysts arise from remnants of the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct in females.

questions.question_text: Nerve supply of the extraocular muscles is constituted by all except?
questions.explanation: Extraocular muscles are supplied by cranial nerves III, IV and VI. The ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve is sensory.

questions.question_text: Claudication due to popliteal-femoral incompetence is primarily seen in?
questions.explanation: Arterial insufficiency involving the femoropopliteal segment commonly causes exertional pain in the calf.

questions.question_text: Which muscle is paralyzed if there is hyperextension of the metacarpophalangeal joint and flexion of the interphalangeal joint?
questions.explanation: The lumbricals and interossei flex the metacarpophalangeal joints and extend the interphalangeal joints. Their paralysis produces clawing of the fingers.

questions.question_text: Tumour of the uncinate process of the pancreas will compress which artery?
questions.explanation: The superior mesenteric vessels are closely related to the uncinate process of the pancreas. The superior mesenteric artery passes anterior to it.

questions.question_text: A boy met with a motorbike accident. CT brain shows injury to the posterior end of the superior temporal gyrus. He is likely to suffer from?
questions.explanation: Damage to the posterior part of the dominant superior temporal gyrus, including Wernicke's area, can cause fluent (Wernicke's) aphasia.

questions.question_text: A 65-year-old lady presents with a vascular injury to the inferior frontal gyrus. Which functional area would mostly be affected?
questions.explanation: The dominant inferior frontal gyrus contains Broca's area, which is involved in motor speech production.

questions.question_text: Where is the highest oxygen concentration present in fetal circulation?
questions.explanation: Oxygenated blood from the placenta travels through the umbilical vein and ductus venosus into the inferior vena cava. The most highly oxygenated blood is actually in the umbilical vein before mixing; among the listed options, the IVC is the intended answer.
